```python
        }

    }

    def analyze(self, rule: FirewallRule) -> List[SecurityFinding]:
        """Analyze a rule for insecure protocols with detailed scoring"""
        findings = []

        # Skip disabled rules
        if rule.disabled:
            return findings

        for service in rule.services:
            service_lower = service.lower().strip()

            for protocol, info in self.INSECURE_PROTOCOLS.items():
                if self._detect_protocol(service_lower, protocol, info):
                    score_breakdown = self._calculate_protocol_score(protocol, info, rule)

                    formula = self._generate_formula(score_breakdown)

                    finding = SecurityFinding(
                        rule_id=rule.id,
                        rule_name=rule.name,
                        issue_type=RuleIssueType.INSECURE_PROTOCOL,
                        risk_level=info['risk'],
                        description=f"Rule allows insecure protocol: {protocol.upper()} (service: {service})",
                        recommendation=info['recommendation'],
                        details={
                            'protocol': protocol,
                            'port': info['port'],
                            'service': service,
                            'detection_method': self._get_detection_method(service_lower, protocol, info)
                        },
                        score=score_breakdown['total_score'],
                        score_breakdown=score_breakdown,
                        calculation_formula=formula
                    )
                    findings.append(finding)
                    break

        return findings

    def _detect_protocol(self, service_str: str, protocol: str, info: Dict) -> bool:
        """Enhanced protocol detection"""
        if 'common_names' in info:
            for name in info['common_names']:
                if name in service_str:
                    return True

        if protocol in service_str:
            return True

        port = info['port']
        port_patterns = [
            f"tcp-{port}", f"tcp_{port}", f"tcp/{port}",
            f"udp-{port}", f"udp_{port}", f"udp/{port}",
            f"port-{port}", f"port_{port}", f"port {port}",
            f":{port}", f"/{port}", f"-{port}-", f"_{port}_", f" {port} "
        ]

        for pattern in port_patterns:
            if pattern in service_str:
                return True

        port_regex = rf'\b{port}\b'
        if re.search(port_regex, service_str):
            if self._is_likely_port_reference(service_str, str(port)):
                return True

        if 'alternate_ports' in info:
            for alt_port in info['alternate_ports']:
                if (f"tcp-{alt_port}" in service_str or
                    f"udp-{alt_port}" in service_str or
                    f"port-{alt_port}" in service_str or
                    f":{alt_port}" in service_str or
                    re.search(rf'\b{alt_port}\b', service_str)):
                    return True

        port_range_pattern = r'(\d+)\s*[-–]\s*(\d+)'
        matches = re.findall(port_range_pattern, service_str)
        for start, end in matches:
            if int(start) <= port <= int(end):
                return True

        return False

    def _is_likely_port_reference(self, service_str: str, port: str) -> bool:
        """Determine if a number is likely referring to a port"""
        port_indicators = [
            'tcp', 'udp', 'port', 'service', 'allow', 'deny',
            'permit', 'block', 'listen', 'connect', 'dst', 'src'
        ]

        service_lower = service_str.lower()
        for indicator in port_indicators:
            if indicator in service_lower:
                return True

        if service_str.strip() == port:
            return True

        if re.search(rf'(^|[^0-9]){port}($|[^0-9])', service_str):
            port_num = int(port)
            if 1 <= port_num <= 65535:
                return True

        return False

    def _get_detection_method(self, service_str: str, protocol: str, info: Dict) -> str:
        """Return how the protocol was detected"""
        if protocol in service_str:
            return f"Protocol name '{protocol}' found"

        port = info['port']
        if f"tcp-{port}" in service_str or f"udp-{port}" in service_str:
            return f"Standard port notation (tcp/udp-{port})"

        if f":{port}" in service_str:
            return f"Port notation (:{port})"

        if re.search(rf'\b{port}\b', service_str):
            return f"Standalone port number {port}"

        if 'common_names' in info:
            for name in info['common_names']:
                if name in service_str:
                    return f"Common service name '{name}'"

        if 'alternate_ports' in info:
            for alt_port in info['alternate_ports']:
                if str(alt_port) in service_str:
                    return f"Alternate port {alt_port}"

        port_range_pattern = r'(\d+)\s*[-–]\s*(\d+)'
        matches = re.findall(port_range_pattern, service_str)
        for start, end in matches:
            if int(start) <= port <= int(end):
                return f"Port range {start}-{end}"

        return "Unknown detection method"

    def _calculate_protocol_score(self, protocol: str, info: Dict, rule: FirewallRule) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Calculate detailed score breakdown for insecure protocol"""
        score_breakdown = {
            'base_score': info['base_score'],
            'factors': {},
            'modifiers': {},
            'calculation_steps': [f"Base score for {protocol.upper()}: {info['base_score']} points"],
            'total_score': info['base_score']
        }

        for factor, points in info['score_factors'].items():
            score_breakdown['factors'][factor] = points
            score_breakdown['calculation_steps'].append(f"{factor.replace('_', ' ').title()}: +{points} points")
            score_breakdown['total_score'] += points

        if 'untrusted' in [zone.lower() for zone in rule.source_zones]:
            score_breakdown['modifiers']['untrusted_source_zone'] = 10
            score_breakdown['calculation_steps'].append("Untrusted source zone: +10 points")
            score_breakdown['total_score'] += 10

        if score_breakdown['total_score'] > 100:
            score_breakdown['calculation_steps'].append(f"Score capped at 100 (was {score_breakdown['total_score']})")
            score_breakdown['total_score'] = 100

        return score_breakdown

    def _generate_formula(self, score_breakdown: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
        """Generate calculation formula from score breakdown"""
        components = [f"Base ({score_breakdown['base_score']})"]
        for factor, points in score_breakdown['factors'].items():
            components.append(f"{factor.replace('_', ' ').title()} ({points})")
        for modifier, points in score_breakdown.get('modifiers', {}).items():
            components.append(f"{modifier.replace('_', ' ').title()} ({points})")
        return f"Score = {' + '.join(components)} = {score_breakdown['total_score']}"
```

## `src/firewall_analyzer/analysis/redundancy.py`

```python
import hashlib
from typing import List

from ..core.models import FirewallRule, SecurityFinding, RuleIssueType, RiskLevel


class RedundancyAnalyzer:
    """Analyzes rules for redundancy and shadowing"""

    def analyze_ruleset(self, rules: List[FirewallRule]) -> List[SecurityFinding]:
        """Analyze entire ruleset for redundancy and shadowing"""
        findings = []
        findings.extend(self._find_duplicate_rules(rules))
        findings.extend(self._find_shadowed_rules(rules))
        return findings

    def _find_duplicate_rules(self, rules: List[FirewallRule]) -> List[SecurityFinding]:
        """Find exact duplicate rules with scoring"""
        findings = []
        rule_signatures = {}

        for rule in rules:
            if rule.disabled:
                continue

            signature = self._create_rule_signature(rule)

            if signature in rule_signatures:
                duplicate_of = rule_signatures[signature]

                score_breakdown = {
                    'base_score': 45,
                    'factors': {
                        'exact_duplicate': 30,
                        'maintenance_overhead': 10,
                        'confusion_risk': 5
                    },
                    'calculation_steps': [
                        'Exact duplicate: 30 points',
                        'Maintenance overhead: 10 points',
                        'Confusion risk: 5 points',
                        'Total: 45 points'
                    ],
                    'total_score': 45
                }

                formula = "Score = 30 (duplicate) + 10 (maintenance) + 5 (confusion) = 45"

                finding = SecurityFinding(
                    rule_id=rule.id,
                    rule_name=rule.name,
                    issue_type=RuleIssueType.REDUNDANT,
                    risk_level=RiskLevel.MEDIUM,
                    description=f"Duplicate rule. Identical to rule '{duplicate_of['name']}' (ID: {duplicate_of['id']})",
                    recommendation="Remove duplicate rule to simplify ruleset and reduce maintenance overhead",
                    details={'duplicate_of': duplicate_of['id'], 'duplicate_name': duplicate_of['name']},
                    score=45,
                    score_breakdown=score_breakdown,
                    calculation_formula=formula
                )
                findings.append(finding)
            else:
                rule_signatures[signature] = {'id': rule.id, 'name': rule.name}

        return findings

    def _find_shadowed_rules(self, rules: List[FirewallRule]) -> List[SecurityFinding]:
        """Find rules that are shadowed by earlier rules with scoring"""
        findings = []

        for i, rule in enumerate(rules):
            if rule.disabled:
                continue

            for j in range(i):
                earlier_rule = rules[j]
                if earlier_rule.disabled:
                    continue

                if self._is_shadowed_by(rule, earlier_rule):
                    score_breakdown = {
                        'base_score': 65,
                        'factors': {
                            'never_matched': 25,
                            'rule_order_issue': 20,
                            'ineffective_rule': 15,
                            'troubleshooting_difficulty': 5
                        },
                        'calculation_steps': [
                            'Never matched: 25 points',
                            'Rule order issue: 20 points',
                            'Ineffective rule: 15 points',
                            'Troubleshooting difficulty: 5 points',
                            'Total: 65 points'
                        ],
                        'total_score': 65
                    }

                    formula = "Score = 25 (never matched) + 20 (order) + 15 (ineffective) + 5 = 65"

                    finding = SecurityFinding(
                        rule_id=rule.id,
                        rule_name=rule.name,
                        issue_type=RuleIssueType.SHADOWED,
                        risk_level=RiskLevel.HIGH,
                        description=f"Rule is shadowed by earlier rule '{earlier_rule.name}' (ID: {earlier_rule.id})",
                        recommendation="Review rule order or remove shadowed rule to avoid confusion",
                        details={'shadowed_by': earlier_rule.id, 'shadowing_rule': earlier_rule.name},
                        score=65,
                        score_breakdown=score_breakdown,
                        calculation_formula=formula
                    )
                    findings.append(finding)
                    break

        return findings

    def _create_rule_signature(self, rule: FirewallRule) -> str:
        """Create a unique signature for a rule"""
        components = [
            ','.join(sorted(rule.source_zones)),
            ','.join(sorted(rule.dest_zones)),
            ','.join(sorted(rule.source_addresses)),
            ','.join(sorted(rule.dest_addresses)),
            ','.join(sorted(rule.services)),
            ','.join(sorted(rule.applications)),
            rule.action
        ]
        return hashlib.md5('|'.join(components).encode()).hexdigest()

    def _is_shadowed_by(self, rule: FirewallRule, earlier_rule: FirewallRule) -> bool:
        """Check if a rule is shadowed by an earlier rule"""
        return (
            self._is_subset(rule.source_zones, earlier_rule.source_zones) and
            self._is_subset(rule.dest_zones, earlier_rule.dest_zones) and
            self._is_subset(rule.source_addresses, earlier_rule.source_addresses) and
            self._is_subset(rule.dest_addresses, earlier_rule.dest_addresses) and
            self._is_subset(rule.services, earlier_rule.services) and
            self._is_subset(rule.applications, earlier_rule.applications)
        )

    def _is_subset(self, list1: List[str], list2: List[str]) -> bool:
        """Check if list1 is a subset of list2 or if list2 contains 'any'"""
        if 'any' in [item.lower() for item in list2]:
            return True
        set1 = set(item.lower() for item in list1)
        set2 = set(item.lower() for item in list2)
        return set1.issubset(set2)
```

## `src/firewall_analyzer/analysis/remote_management_checker.py`

```python
"""
Remote Management check - flags ALLOW rules that expose remote-management access.

Logic follows the decision flowchart:
  1. Only ALLOW rules are considered.
  2. If Application is in the remote-access APP list      -> match type APPLICATION (high confidence)
  3. Else if a remote-access PORT appears in the Service   -> match type PORT      (medium confidence)
  4. If App = any AND Service = any                        -> BROAD RULE RISK      (low confidence)

Risk mapping:
  - BROAD RULE (any/any)                 -> CRITICAL
  - Remote access allowed from ANY source-> CRITICAL
  - Remote access from a specific source -> MEDIUM

Note: UDP 514 = Syslog, NOT RSH -> excluded from port matching.
"""
from .base import BaseAnalyzer
from ..core.models import SecurityFinding, RuleIssueType, RiskLevel


# A. Remote access APPLICATION list (Palo Alto App-IDs). '-' prefix handles gotomypc-*, etc.
REMOTE_ACCESS_APPS = [
    "ssh", "ms-rdp", "rdp", "logmein", "vnc-base", "vnc", "rsh", "telnet",
    "teamviewer", "anydesk", "gotomypc", "splashtop", "beyondtrust",
    "winrm", "rlogin", "rexec", "pcanywhere", "radmin", "xdmcp", "x11",
]

# B. Remote access PORT list -> protocol name.
REMOTE_ACCESS_PORTS = {
    "22": "SSH", "23": "Telnet", "3389": "RDP", "5900": "VNC",
    "514": "RSH", "513": "rlogin", "512": "rexec",
    "5985": "WinRM (HTTP)", "5986": "WinRM (HTTPS)",
    "177": "XDMCP", "3283": "Apple Remote Desktop",
}
X11_RANGE = range(6000, 6064)  # X11 uses 6000-6063


def _is_any(values):
    return any(str(v).lower() == "any" for v in values)


def _app_matches(applications):
    matched = []
    for app in applications:
        al = str(app).lower()
        for known in REMOTE_ACCESS_APPS:
            if al == known or al.startswith(known + "-") or known in al:
                matched.append(known)
                break
    return sorted(set(matched))


def _port_matches(services):
    """Match remote-access ports in the service field. Skips UDP 514 (Syslog)."""
    matched = []
    for svc in services:
        s = str(svc).lower()
        is_udp_514 = ("udp" in s and "514" in s)
        token = s.replace("tcp", " ").replace("udp", " ").replace("/", " ").replace(":", " ")
        for part in token.split():
            if not part.isdigit():
                continue
            if part == "514" and is_udp_514:
                continue  # syslog, not rsh
            if part in REMOTE_ACCESS_PORTS:
                matched.append(REMOTE_ACCESS_PORTS[part])
            else:
                try:
                    if int(part) in X11_RANGE:
                        matched.append("X11")
                except ValueError:
                    pass
    return sorted(set(matched))


class RemoteManagementAnalyzer(BaseAnalyzer):
    """Flags ALLOW rules that expose remote-management access (app / port / broad)."""

    def analyze(self, rule):
        findings = []

        if rule.action.lower() != "allow":
            return findings

        app_any = _is_any(rule.applications)
        svc_any = _is_any(rule.services)
        src_any = _is_any(rule.source_addresses)

        match_type, matched = None, []

        # 1) APPLICATION match (highest confidence)
        app_hits = _app_matches(rule.applications)
        if app_hits:
            match_type, matched = "APPLICATION", app_hits

        # 2) PORT match (medium confidence) - only if no app match
        if not matched:
            port_hits = _port_matches(rule.services)
            if port_hits:
                match_type, matched = "PORT", port_hits

        if not matched:
            return findings

        protos = ", ".join(matched)

        # Risk + score
        if match_type == "BROAD RULE":
            level, base, extra = RiskLevel.CRITICAL, 60, 40
        elif src_any:
            level, base, extra = RiskLevel.CRITICAL, 50, 40
        else:
            level, base, extra = RiskLevel.MEDIUM, 40, 0
        total = base + extra

        suffix = " from ANY source!" if (src_any and match_type != "BROAD RULE") else ""
        print(f"REMOTE-MGMT [{match_type}] : '{rule.name}' allows {protos}{suffix}")

        findings.append(SecurityFinding(
            rule_id=rule.id,
            rule_name=rule.name,
            issue_type=RuleIssueType.MANAGEMENT_ACCESS,
            risk_level=level,
            description=f"Rule allows remote management ({match_type} match: {protos}).",
            recommendation=(
                f"Restrict '{rule.name}' to specific administrator source IPs, "
                f"use secure protocols over VPN, and avoid 'any' source. "
                f"Review broad rules manually."
            ),
            details={"match_type": match_type, "protocols": matched, "any_source": src_any},
            score=total,
            calculation_formula=f"Score = {base} + {extra} = {total}",
        ))
        return findings
```

## `src/firewall_analyzer/analysis/security_profiles.py`

```python
from ..core.models import SecurityFinding, RuleIssueType, RiskLevel


class SecurityProfileAnalyzer:
    """Checks whether each ALLOW/ACCEPT rule has security profiles applied.
    Works for any CSV (FortiGate multi-column, Palo Alto single-column, etc.)."""

    # All possible profile column names across vendors
    PROFILE_COLUMNS = [
        "AVProfile", "IPSProfile", "WebFilterProfile",
        "ApplicationControlProfile", "SSLSSHProfile",
        "Security Profile", "SecurityProfile", "Profile",
    ]

    def _is_empty(self, value):
        if value is None:
            return True
        v = str(value).strip().lower()
        return v in ("", "-", "--", "n/a", "none")

    def _get_all_profiles(self, rule):
        """Collect unique 'ColumnName=value' pairs, avoiding duplicate columns/values."""
        raw = rule.raw_data or {}

        found = []
        seen_columns = set()   # avoid same normalized column twice
        seen_pairs = set()     # avoid identical column=value twice

        for col in self.PROFILE_COLUMNS:
            # normalize the column name to avoid "Security Profile" == "SecurityProfile"
            norm_col = col.lower().replace(" ", "").replace("_", "")
            if norm_col in seen_columns:
                continue

            # find the value for this column (exact, then flexible)
            value = raw.get(col)
            if value is None:
                for k, v in raw.items():
                    if str(k).lower().replace(" ", "").replace("_", "") == norm_col:
                        value = v
                        break

            if not self._is_empty(value):
                pair = f"{col}={str(value).strip()}"
                if pair not in seen_pairs:
                    seen_pairs.add(pair)
                    seen_columns.add(norm_col)
                    found.append(pair)

        return found

    def analyze_ruleset(self, rules):
        findings = []
        seen_rule_ids = set()   # avoid duplicate rules

        print("=== Security Profile check ===")

        for rule in rules:
            # Only ALLOW/ACCEPT rules
            if rule.action.lower() not in ("allow", "accept"):
                continue

            # Avoid processing the same rule twice
            if rule.id in seen_rule_ids:
                continue
            seen_rule_ids.add(rule.id)

            profiles = self._get_all_profiles(rule)

            # Show rules that HAVE at least one profile
            if profiles:
                profile_str = ", ".join(profiles)
                print(f"[HAS PROFILE] {rule.name} -> {profile_str}")
                findings.append(
                    SecurityFinding(
                        rule_id=rule.id,
                        rule_name=rule.name,
                        issue_type=RuleIssueType.MISCONFIGURED,
                        risk_level=RiskLevel.LOW,
                        description=f"HASPROFILE: Rule '{rule.name}' has security profiles: {profile_str}",
                        recommendation="No action needed. Security profiles are applied.",
                        details={"security_profile": profile_str},
                        score=1
                    )
                )

        print(f"Total ALLOW rules WITH security profiles: {len(findings)}")
        return findings
```

## `src/firewall_analyzer/analysis/zone_analyzer.py`

```python
from typing import List, Dict, Any, Optional

from ..core.models import FirewallRule
from ..utils.ip_utils import IPAddressUtils


class ZoneBasedAnalyzer:
    """Analyzes firewall rules by network zones"""

    def __init__(self, zone_config: Dict):
        self.zones = zone_config.get('zones', {})
        self._build_subnet_to_zone_mapping()

    def _build_subnet_to_zone_mapping(self):
        """Build mapping of subnets to zones for fast lookup"""
        self.subnet_to_zone = {}
        self.all_subnets = []

        for zone_id, zone_data in self.zones.items():
            for subnet in zone_data.get('subnets', []):
                self.subnet_to_zone[subnet] = zone_id
                self.all_subnets.append(subnet)

    def identify_zone_for_address(self, address: str) -> Optional[str]:
        """Identify which zone an IP address belongs to"""
        if address.lower() in ['any', 'all', '*', '0.0.0.0']:
            return 'external'

        for subnet in self.all_subnets:
            if IPAddressUtils.ip_in_subnet(address, subnet):
                return self.subnet_to_zone[subnet]

        return None

    def identify_zone_for_subnet(self, subnet: str) -> Optional[str]:
        """Identify which zone a subnet belongs to"""
        if subnet.lower() in ['any', 'all', '*', '0.0.0.0']:
            return 'external'

        if subnet in self.subnet_to_zone:
            return self.subnet_to_zone[subnet]

        for zone_subnet in self.all_subnets:
            overlap = IPAddressUtils.subnet_overlap_check(subnet, zone_subnet)
            if overlap['overlaps']:
                return self.subnet_to_zone[zone_subnet]

        return None

    def get_rules_for_zone_pair(self, rules: List[FirewallRule],
                               source_zone: str, dest_zone: str) -> List[FirewallRule]:
        """Get all rules for specific source → destination zone pair"""
        matching_rules = []

        for rule in rules:
            rule_source_zones = set()
            rule_dest_zones = set()

            for addr in rule.source_addresses:
                zone = self.identify_zone_for_address(addr) or self.identify_zone_for_subnet(addr)
                if zone:
                    rule_source_zones.add(zone)

            for addr in rule.dest_addresses:
                zone = self.identify_zone_for_address(addr) or self.identify_zone_for_subnet(addr)
                if zone:
                    rule_dest_zones.add(zone)

            if (source_zone in rule_source_zones or source_zone == 'any') and \
               (dest_zone in rule_dest_zones or dest_zone == 'any'):
                matching_rules.append(rule)

        return matching_rules

    def get_rules_for_ip(self, rules: List[FirewallRule], ip_address: str) -> List[FirewallRule]:
        """Get all rules connected to specific IP address or subnet"""
        matching_rules = []

        for rule in rules:
            for addr in rule.source_addresses + rule.dest_addresses:
                if IPAddressUtils.ip_in_subnet(ip_address, addr):
                    matching_rules.append(rule)
                    break

        return matching_rules

    def get_zone_summary(self, rules: List[FirewallRule]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Generate summary of rules by zone pair"""
        zone_summary = {}

        for rule in rules:
            source_zones = set()
            dest_zones = set()

            for addr in rule.source_addresses:
                zone = self.identify_zone_for_address(addr) or self.identify_zone_for_subnet(addr)
                if zone:
                    source_zones.add(zone)

            for addr in rule.dest_addresses:
                zone = self.identify_zone_for_address(addr) or self.identify_zone_for_subnet(addr)
                if zone:
                    dest_zones.add(zone)

            for src_zone in source_zones:
                for dst_zone in dest_zones:
                    pair = f"{src_zone} → {dst_zone}"
                    if pair not in zone_summary:
                        zone_summary[pair] = {
                            'allow_rules': 0,
                            'deny_rules': 0,
                            'total_rules': 0,
                            'rules': []
                        }

                    if rule.action.lower() == 'allow':
                        zone_summary[pair]['allow_rules'] += 1
                    else:
                        zone_summary[pair]['deny_rules'] += 1

                    zone_summary[pair]['total_rules'] += 1
                    zone_summary[pair]['rules'].append(rule.id)

        return zone_summary
```

```python
    def __init__(self, config_dir: str = "."):
        self.config_dir = config_dir
        self.field_mapping_config = None
        self.zone_config = None
        self.analysis_config = None

    def load_field_mapping_config(self, config_file: str = None) -> Dict:
        """Load field mapping configuration from JSON file or use default"""
        if config_file and os.path.exists(config_file):
            try:
                with open(config_file, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
                    self.field_mapping_config = json.load(f)
                    return self.field_mapping_config
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"Warning: Error loading field mapping config: {e}")
                print("Using default configuration...")
                self.field_mapping_config = self.DEFAULT_FIELD_MAPPING_SCHEMA
                return self.field_mapping_config
        else:
            self.field_mapping_config = self.DEFAULT_FIELD_MAPPING_SCHEMA
            return self.field_mapping_config

    def load_zone_config(self, config_file: str = None) -> Dict:
        """Load zone configuration from JSON file or use default"""
        if config_file and os.path.exists(config_file):
            try:
                with open(config_file, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
                    self.zone_config = json.load(f)
                    return self.zone_config
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"Warning: Error loading zone config: {e}")
                print("Using default configuration...")
                self.zone_config = self.DEFAULT_ZONE_CONFIG
                return self.zone_config
        else:
            self.zone_config = self.DEFAULT_ZONE_CONFIG
            return self.zone_config

    def save_default_configs(self, output_dir: str = "."):
        """Save default configuration templates to JSON files"""
        os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)

        field_mapping_file = os.path.join(output_dir, "field_mapping_schema.json")
        zone_config_file = os.path.join(output_dir, "zone_config.json")
        analysis_config_file = os.path.join(output_dir, "analysis_config.json")

        try:
            with open(field_mapping_file, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
                json.dump(self.DEFAULT_FIELD_MAPPING_SCHEMA, f, indent=2)
            print(f"✓ Field mapping schema template saved: {field_mapping_file}")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error saving field mapping schema: {e}")

        try:
            with open(zone_config_file, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
                json.dump(self.DEFAULT_ZONE_CONFIG, f, indent=2)
            print(f"✓ Zone configuration template saved: {zone_config_file}")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error saving zone config: {e}")

        try:
            with open(analysis_config_file, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
                json.dump(self.analysis_config or self._default_analysis_config(), f, indent=2)
            print(f"✓ Analysis configuration template saved: {analysis_config_file}")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error saving analysis config: {e}")

    def get_vendor_schema(self, vendor_type: VendorType) -> Dict:
        """Get vendor-specific schema from configuration"""
        if not self.field_mapping_config:
            self.load_field_mapping_config()

        vendor_value = vendor_type.value
        if vendor_value in self.field_mapping_config.get('vendors', {}):
            return self.field_mapping_config['vendors'][vendor_value]

        return self.field_mapping_config['vendors'].get('generic', {})

    def get_zones(self) -> Dict:
        """Get all configured zones"""
        if not self.zone_config:
            self.load_zone_config()

        return self.zone_config.get('zones', {})

    def load_analysis_config(self, config_file: str = None) -> Dict:
        """Load analysis configuration or fall back to defaults"""
        if self.analysis_config and not config_file:
            return self.analysis_config

        candidate_paths = []
        if config_file:
            candidate_paths.append(config_file)
        if self.config_dir:
            candidate_paths.append(os.path.join(self.config_dir, "analysis_config.json"))
        module_default = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "analysis_config.json")
        if module_default not in candidate_paths:
            candidate_paths.append(module_default)

        for path in candidate_paths:
            if not path:
                continue
            if os.path.exists(path):
                try:
                    with open(path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
                        self.analysis_config = json.load(f)
                        return self.analysis_config
                except Exception as e:
                    print(f"Warning: Error loading analysis config from {path}: {e}")

        print("Warning: Analysis configuration not found - using defaults")
        self.analysis_config = self._default_analysis_config()
        return self.analysis_config

    def _default_analysis_config(self) -> Dict:
        """Return a deep copy of the default analysis configuration"""
        return copy.deepcopy(self.DEFAULT_ANALYSIS_CONFIG)
```

```python
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum
from typing import Dict, List, Any

# ============================================================================
# Enumerations
# ============================================================================


class VendorType(Enum):
    """Supported firewall vendors"""
    PALO_ALTO = "palo_alto"
    CISCO_ASA = "cisco_asa"
    FORTINET = "fortinet"
    CHECKPOINT = "checkpoint"
    JUNIPER_SRX = "juniper_srx"
    GENERIC = "generic"


class RiskLevel(Enum):
    """Risk level enumeration for security assessment"""
    CRITICAL = "critical"
    HIGH = "high"
    MEDIUM = "medium"
    LOW = "low"
    INFO = "info"


class RuleIssueType(Enum):
    """Types of issues that can be found in firewall rules"""
    OVERLY_PERMISSIVE = "overly_permissive"
    INSECURE_PROTOCOL = "insecure_protocol"
    APPLICATION_RISK = "application_risk"
    REDUNDANT = "redundant"
    SHADOWED = "shadowed"
    UNUSED = "unused"
    DISABLED = "disabled"
    MISSING_LOGGING = "missing_logging"
    WEAK_AUTHENTICATION = "weak_authentication"
    EXPIRED = "expired"
    MISCONFIGURED = "misconfigured"
    MANAGEMENT_ACCESS = "management_access"
    LATERAL_MOVEMENT = "lateral_movement"
    UNENCRYPTED_TRAFFIC = "unencrypted_traffic"
    BROAD_APPLICATION_ALLOW = "broad_application_allow"
    WEAK_CRYPTO = "weak_crypto"
    MISSING_TIME_RESTRICTIONS = "missing_time_restrictions"


# ============================================================================
# Data Models
# ============================================================================


@dataclass
class SecurityFinding:
    """Represents a security finding for a rule"""
    rule_id: str
    rule_name: str
    issue_type: RuleIssueType
    risk_level: RiskLevel
    description: str
    recommendation: str
    details: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    score: int = 0
    score_breakdown: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    calculation_formula: str = ""


@dataclass
class FirewallRule:
    """Structured representation of a firewall rule"""
    id: str
    name: str
    source_zones: List[str]
    dest_zones: List[str]
    source_addresses: List[str]
    dest_addresses: List[str]
    source_users: List[str]
    services: List[str]
    applications: List[str]
    action: str
    disabled: bool
    rule_usage: str
    modified: str
    raw_data: Dict[str, str]
    logging: str = ''
    findings: List[SecurityFinding] = field(default_factory=list)
    risk_score: int = 0
    score_breakdown: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    vendor_type: VendorType = VendorType.GENERIC
```

```python
import json
import re
from typing import List, Dict


class PaloAltoAppIDHandler:
    """Loads and manages Palo Alto AppID database for service-to-port mapping"""

    def __init__(self, app_id_file: str = "palo_alto_applipedia.json"):
        self.app_id_database = {}
        self.app_name_to_ports = {}
        self.app_metadata_by_name = {}
        self.load_app_id_database(app_id_file)

    def load_app_id_database(self, app_id_file: str):
        """Load Palo Alto AppID database from JSON file"""
        try:
            with open(app_id_file, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
                apps = json.load(f)

            if not isinstance(apps, list):
                apps = [apps]

            for app in apps:
                app_id = app.get('id')
                ports = self._extract_ports_from_app(app)
                metadata = self._build_metadata(app, ports)

                # Index by ID
                if app_id:
                    self.app_id_database[str(app_id)] = metadata

                # Index by every alias (name, appName_js, sanitized variants)
                for alias in metadata['aliases']:
                    self.app_name_to_ports[alias] = ports
                    self.app_metadata_by_name[alias] = metadata

            print(f"✓ Loaded {len(self.app_id_database)} applications from Palo Alto AppID database")

        except FileNotFoundError:
            print(f"⚠ Warning: Palo Alto AppID database file '{app_id_file}' not found")
            print("  Service names will not be converted to ports")
        except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
            print(f"⚠ Warning: Error parsing AppID database: {e}")

    def _extract_ports_from_app(self, app: Dict) -> List[str]:
        """Extract port information from app definition"""
        ports = []

        # Check standard_ports in characteristics
        if 'characteristics' in app:
            characteristics = app['characteristics']
            if isinstance(characteristics, dict):
                standard_ports_str = characteristics.get('standard_ports', '')
            else:
                standard_ports_str = str(characteristics)

            # Parse port information like "tcp/3468,6346,11300" or "tcp/80,443"
            if standard_ports_str:
                # Extract just the port part
                port_match = re.search(r'(tcp|udp)/([\d,\-/]+)', standard_ports_str, re.IGNORECASE)
                if port_match:
                    protocol = port_match.group(1).lower()
                    port_spec = port_match.group(2)

                    # Parse individual ports and ranges
                    port_items = port_spec.split(',')
                    for item in port_items:
                        item = item.strip()
                        if '-' in item:
                            # Port range like 1560-1591
                            try:
                                start, end = item.split('-')
                                ports.append(f"{protocol}/{item}")
                            except ValueError:
                                ports.append(f"{protocol}/{item}")
                        else:
                            # Single port
                            ports.append(f"{protocol}/{item}")

        return ports if ports else ['any']

    def _build_metadata(self, app: Dict, ports: List[str]) -> Dict:
        """Create normalized metadata entry for an application"""
        characteristics = app.get('characteristics', {}) or {}
        risk_value = self._parse_risk_value(app.get('risk') or characteristics.get('risk'))

        display_name = (app.get('name') or '').strip()
        app_js = (app.get('appName_js') or '').strip()

        metadata = {
            'id': app.get('id'),
            'display_name': display_name or app_js,
            'app_name_js': app_js,
            'ports': ports,
            'category': app.get('category') or characteristics.get('category', ''),
            'subcategory': app.get('subcategory') or characteristics.get('subcategory', ''),
            'technology': app.get('technology') or characteristics.get('technology', ''),
            'risk': risk_value,
            'description': app.get('description', ''),
            'references': app.get('references', []),
            'raw': app,
            'aliases': self._generate_aliases(display_name, app_js)
        }

        return metadata

    def _generate_aliases(self, *names: str) -> List[str]:
        """Generate a list of normalized aliases for lookup"""
        aliases = set()

        for name in names:
            if not name:
                continue
            lowered = name.strip().lower()
            if not lowered:
                continue
            aliases.add(self._normalize_key(lowered))

            # Add variants
            variants = {
                lowered.replace(' ', ''),
                lowered.replace(' ', '-'),
                lowered.replace(' ', '_'),
                lowered.replace('-', ''),
                lowered.replace('_', ''),
                lowered.replace('-', '_'),
                lowered.replace('_', '-')
            }

            aliases.update(self._normalize_key(variant) for variant in variants if variant)

        return list(aliases)

    @staticmethod
    def _normalize_key(value: str) -> str:
        """Normalize lookup keys for consistent matching"""
        return value.strip().lower()

    @staticmethod
    def _parse_risk_value(value) -> int:
        """Normalize risk value to int between 0-5"""
        if isinstance(value, int):
            return value
        if isinstance(value, str):
            digits = ''.join(ch for ch in value if ch.isdigit())
            if digits:
                try:
                    return int(digits)
                except ValueError:
                    return 0
        return 0

    def get_ports_for_service(self, service_name: str) -> List[str]:
        """Get ports for a given service name"""
        normalized = self._normalize_key(service_name)

        # Direct alias lookup
        if normalized in self.app_name_to_ports:
            return self.app_name_to_ports[normalized]

        # Partial / contains matching
        for alias, ports in self.app_name_to_ports.items():
            if alias in normalized or normalized in alias:
                return ports

        metadata = self.get_application_metadata(service_name)
        if metadata:
            return metadata.get('ports', ['any'])

        # Not found in database
        return [service_name]

    def resolve_services_to_ports(self, services: List[str]) -> List[str]:
        """Convert service names to ports (annotated with original service)"""
        resolved_ports = []

        for service in services:
            service_normalized = service.strip()
            if not service_normalized:
                continue

            if service_normalized.lower() == 'any':
                resolved_ports.append('any')
                continue

            ports = self.get_ports_for_service(service_normalized)
            metadata = self.get_application_metadata(service_normalized)
            display_label = service_normalized
            if metadata:
                display_label = metadata.get('display_name') or metadata.get('app_name_js') or service_normalized

            # If AppID lookup failed, keep the original value
            if len(ports) == 1 and ports[0] == service_normalized:
                resolved_ports.append(display_label)
                continue

            for port in ports:
                resolved_ports.append(f"{display_label} ({port})")

        # Remove duplicates while maintaining order
        seen = set()
        unique_ports = []
        for port in resolved_ports:
            if port not in seen:
                seen.add(port)
                unique_ports.append(port)

        return unique_ports if unique_ports else ['any']

    def get_application_metadata(self, application_name: str) -> Dict:
        """Return metadata for an application name if available"""
        if not application_name:
            return {}

        normalized = self._normalize_key(application_name)

        if normalized in self.app_metadata_by_name:
            return self.app_metadata_by_name[normalized]

        for alias, metadata in self.app_metadata_by_name.items():
            if alias in normalized or normalized in alias:
                return metadata

        return {}

    def get_application_risk(self, application_name: str) -> int:
        """Get Palo Alto risk rating (0-5) for an application"""
        metadata = self.get_application_metadata(application_name)
        return metadata.get('risk', 0) if metadata else 0
```

## `src/firewall_analyzer/data/parser.py`

```python
import csv
import hashlib
from typing import List, Dict, Any, Optional

from ..config.manager import ConfigurationManager
from ..core.models import VendorType, FirewallRule
from .appid_handler import PaloAltoAppIDHandler


class SchemaNormalizer:
    """Normalize firewall rule data from different vendor formats to a common schema"""

    def __init__(self, vendor_type: VendorType = VendorType.GENERIC,
                 config_manager: ConfigurationManager = None,
                 app_id_handler: PaloAltoAppIDHandler = None):
        self.vendor_type = vendor_type
        self.config_manager = config_manager or ConfigurationManager()
        self.app_id_handler = app_id_handler
        self.schema = self.config_manager.get_vendor_schema(vendor_type)
        self.field_mappings = self.schema['field_mappings']

    def detect_vendor(self, fieldnames: List[str]) -> VendorType:
        """Auto-detect vendor type based on field names"""
        fieldnames_lower = [f.lower().replace(' ', '_').replace('-', '_') for f in fieldnames]

        palo_alto_indicators = ['column1', 'source_zone', 'destination_zone', 'source_address']
        if all(indicator in fieldnames_lower for indicator in palo_alto_indicators[:3]):
            return VendorType.PALO_ALTO

        cisco_indicators = ['access_list', 'source', 'destination', 'protocol']
        if any(indicator in fieldnames_lower for indicator in cisco_indicators):
            return VendorType.CISCO_ASA

        # FortiGate detection: match the actual export headers (PolicyID, SrcZone, etc.)
        fortinet_indicators = ['policyid', 'srczone', 'dstzone', 'sourceaddress', 'destinationaddress']
        if all(indicator in fieldnames_lower for indicator in fortinet_indicators):
            return VendorType.FORTINET

        checkpoint_indicators = ['rule_number', 'source', 'destination', 'service']
        if all(indicator in fieldnames_lower for indicator in checkpoint_indicators):
            return VendorType.CHECKPOINT

        juniper_indicators = ['from_zone', 'to_zone', 'source_address', 'destination_address']
        if all(indicator in fieldnames_lower for indicator in juniper_indicators):
            return VendorType.JUNIPER_SRX

        return VendorType.GENERIC

    def normalize_row(self, row: Dict[str, str]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Normalize a single row of firewall rule data"""
        normalized = {}

        for normalized_field, vendor_field in self.field_mappings.items():
            vendor_field_lower = vendor_field.lower().replace(' ', '_').replace('-', '_')
            value = None

            if vendor_field in row:
                value = row[vendor_field]
            else:
                for field_name, field_value in row.items():
                    field_name_normalized = field_name.lower().replace(' ', '_').replace('-', '_')
                    if field_name_normalized == vendor_field_lower:
                        value = field_value
                        break

            normalized[normalized_field] = value if value is not None else ''

        normalized = self._apply_vendor_transformations(normalized, row)
        return normalized

    def _apply_vendor_transformations(self, normalized: Dict[str, Any],
                                     original_row: Dict[str, str]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Apply vendor-specific data transformations"""
        if self.vendor_type == VendorType.PALO_ALTO or (self.app_id_handler and self.vendor_type == VendorType.GENERIC):
            # Handle Palo Alto specific transformations

            if 'disabled' in normalized and normalized['disabled']:
                # Check for [Disabled] marker in the rule name or disabled field
                normalized['disabled'] = '[Disabled]' in normalized['disabled'] or \
                                        normalized['disabled'].lower() == 'yes'
            else:
                normalized['disabled'] = False

            for field in ['source_zones', 'dest_zones', 'source_addresses', 'dest_addresses',
                         'source_users', 'services', 'applications']:
                if normalized.get(field):
                    normalized[field] = self._parse_multiple_values(normalized[field])
                else:
                    normalized[field] = ['any']

            # Convert service names to ports using AppID database
            if self.app_id_handler and normalized.get('services'):
                normalized['services'] = self.app_id_handler.resolve_services_to_ports(normalized['services'])

        elif self.vendor_type == VendorType.CISCO_ASA:
            if 'disabled' in normalized and normalized['disabled']:
                normalized['disabled'] = normalized['disabled'].lower() == 'inactive'
            else:
                normalized['disabled'] = False

            for field in ['source_addresses', 'dest_addresses']:
                if normalized.get(field):
                    normalized[field] = self._parse_multiple_values(normalized[field])
                else:
                    normalized[field] = ['any']

            if normalized.get('services'):
                normalized['services'] = self._parse_multiple_values(normalized['services'])
            else:
                normalized['services'] = ['any']

        elif self.vendor_type == VendorType.FORTINET:
            # FIX: 'disabled' now maps to the FortiGate "Enabled" column (TRUE = enabled,
            # FALSE = disabled) which is INVERTED vs a "Disabled" column. So the rule is
            # disabled only when the value is FALSE/no/0/disable.
            enabled_val = str(normalized.get('disabled', '')).strip().lower()
            if enabled_val == '':
                # No value -> assume the rule is active (enabled)
                normalized['disabled'] = False
            else:
                normalized['disabled'] = enabled_val in ['false', 'no', '0', 'disable', 'disabled']

            # FIX: include 'applications' so app-risk analysis works on FortiGate
            for field in ['source_zones', 'dest_zones', 'source_addresses',
                          'dest_addresses', 'services', 'applications']:
                if normalized.get(field):
                    normalized[field] = self._parse_multiple_values(normalized[field])
                else:
                    normalized[field] = ['any']

            # FIX: 'rule_usage' now maps to HitCount. Convert to used/unused so the
            # unused-rule detector (which checks for 'unused') keeps working.
            hitcount = str(normalized.get('rule_usage', '')).strip()
            if hitcount.isdigit():
                normalized['rule_usage'] = 'unused' if int(hitcount) == 0 else 'used'

        elif self.vendor_type == VendorType.CHECKPOINT:
            if 'disabled' in normalized and normalized['disabled']:
                normalized['disabled'] = normalized['disabled'].lower() != 'true'
            else:
                normalized['disabled'] = False

            for field in ['source_addresses', 'dest_addresses', 'services']:
                if normalized.get(field):
                    normalized[field] = self._parse_multiple_values(normalized[field])
                else:
                    normalized[field] = ['any']

        elif self.vendor_type == VendorType.JUNIPER_SRX:
            for field in ['source_zones', 'dest_zones', 'source_addresses', 'dest_addresses', 'applications']:
                if normalized.get(field):
                    normalized[field] = self._parse_multiple_values(normalized[field])
                else:
                    normalized[field] = ['any']

        else:
            for field in ['source_zones', 'dest_zones', 'source_addresses', 'dest_addresses',
                         'source_users', 'services', 'applications']:
                if normalized.get(field):
                    normalized[field] = self._parse_multiple_values(normalized[field])
                else:
                    normalized[field] = ['any']

            if 'disabled' in normalized:
                normalized['disabled'] = str(normalized['disabled']).lower() in \
                                        ['true', 'yes', '1', 'enabled'] or \
                                        '[Disabled]' in str(normalized['disabled'])
            else:
                normalized['disabled'] = False

        for field in ['source_zones', 'dest_zones', 'source_addresses', 'dest_addresses',
                     'source_users', 'services', 'applications', 'action']:
            if field not in normalized or not normalized[field]:
                if field in ['source_zones', 'dest_zones', 'source_addresses',
                            'dest_addresses', 'source_users', 'services', 'applications']:
                    normalized[field] = ['any']
                else:
                    normalized[field] = 'allow'

        # FIX: Universal action normalization so every analyzer can rely on
        # 'allow'/'deny'. FortiGate uses ACCEPT/DENY, others use permit/drop/etc.
        action_val = str(normalized.get('action', '')).strip().lower()
        action_map = {
            'accept': 'allow', 'permit': 'allow', 'allow': 'allow', 'pass': 'allow',
            'deny': 'deny', 'drop': 'deny', 'reject': 'deny', 'block': 'deny',
        }
        normalized['action'] = action_map.get(action_val, action_val if action_val else 'allow')

        if 'rule_id' not in normalized or not normalized['rule_id']:
            normalized['rule_id'] = hashlib.md5(str(original_row).encode()).hexdigest()[:8]

        if 'name' not in normalized or not normalized['name']:
            normalized['name'] = f"Rule_{normalized['rule_id']}"

        return normalized

    def _parse_multiple_values(self, value_string: str) -> List[str]:
        """Parse values that may contain multiple items separated by common delimiters"""
        if not value_string or value_string.lower() in ['any', 'all']:
            return ['any']

        delimiters = [';', ',', '|', '\n']
        values = [value_string]

        for delimiter in delimiters:
            new_values = []
            for value in values:
                new_values.extend(value.split(delimiter))
            values = new_values

        cleaned_values = []
        for item in values:
            item = item.strip()
            if item and item.lower() not in ['', 'none', 'null']:
                cleaned_values.append(item)

        return cleaned_values if cleaned_values else ['any']


class MultiVendorCSVParser:
    """Parse CSV files from different firewall vendors into normalized FirewallRule objects"""

    def __init__(self, vendor_type: VendorType = None, config_manager: ConfigurationManager = None,
                 use_hashed=True, debug=False, app_id_handler: PaloAltoAppIDHandler = None):
        self.vendor_type = vendor_type
        self.config_manager = config_manager or ConfigurationManager()
        self.app_id_handler = app_id_handler
        self.use_hashed = use_hashed
        self.debug = debug
        self.schema_normalizer = None
        self.hashed_columns = {}

    def parse_csv(self, csv_file_path: str) -> List[FirewallRule]:
        """Parse CSV file into normalized FirewallRule objects"""
        rules = []

        with open(csv_file_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8-sig') as csvfile:
            reader = csv.DictReader(csvfile)

            if self.vendor_type is None:
                self.vendor_type = self._detect_vendor_from_headers(reader.fieldnames)
                if self.debug:
                    print(f"Auto-detected vendor: {self.vendor_type.value}")

            self.schema_normalizer = SchemaNormalizer(self.vendor_type, self.config_manager, self.app_id_handler)
            self.hashed_columns = self._detect_hashed_columns(reader.fieldnames)

            for row in reader:
                normalized_data = self.schema_normalizer.normalize_row(row)

                rule = FirewallRule(
                    id=normalized_data['rule_id'],
                    name=normalized_data['name'],
                    source_zones=normalized_data['source_zones'],
                    dest_zones=normalized_data['dest_zones'],
                    source_addresses=normalized_data['source_addresses'],
                    dest_addresses=normalized_data['dest_addresses'],
                    source_users=normalized_data.get('source_users', ['any']),
                    services=normalized_data['services'],
                    applications=normalized_data.get('applications', ['any']),
                    action=normalized_data['action'],
                    disabled=normalized_data.get('disabled', False),
                    rule_usage=normalized_data.get('rule_usage', ''),
                    modified=normalized_data.get('modified', ''),
                    logging=normalized_data.get('logging', ''),
                    raw_data=row,
                    vendor_type=self.vendor_type
                )
                rules.append(rule)

        return rules

    def _detect_vendor_from_headers(self, fieldnames: List[str]) -> VendorType:
        """Detect vendor type from CSV headers"""
        return self.schema_normalizer.detect_vendor(fieldnames) if self.schema_normalizer \
               else SchemaNormalizer().detect_vendor(fieldnames)

    def _detect_hashed_columns(self, fieldnames):
        """Detect columns that have hashed counterparts"""
        hashed_mapping = {}
        regular_columns = []
        hashed_columns_list = []

        for field in fieldnames:
            if 'hashed' in field.lower() or '_hash' in field.lower():
                hashed_columns_list.append(field)
            else:
                regular_columns.append(field)

        for regular in regular_columns:
            for hashed in hashed_columns_list:
                regular_clean = regular.lower().replace(' ', '_').replace('-', '_')
                hashed_clean = hashed.lower().replace(' ', '_').replace('-', '_')

                if regular_clean in hashed_clean:
                    hashed_mapping[regular] = hashed
                    if self.debug:
                        print(f"Mapped '{regular}' to hashed column '{hashed}'")

        return hashed_mapping
```

```python
from collections import defaultdict
from typing import List, Dict, Any

from ..core.models import SecurityFinding


class FindingGrouper:
    """Groups and aggregates findings by rule name and other criteria"""

    @staticmethod
    def group_findings_by_rule_name(findings: List[SecurityFinding]) -> Dict[str, List[SecurityFinding]]:
        """Group findings by rule name"""
        grouped = defaultdict(list)
        for finding in findings:
            grouped[finding.rule_name].append(finding)
        return dict(grouped)

    @staticmethod
    def get_findings_summary_by_rule(findings: List[SecurityFinding]) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Get summary statistics for findings grouped by rule"""
        summary = {}
        for finding in findings:
            if finding.rule_name not in summary:
                summary[finding.rule_name] = {
                    'rule_id': finding.rule_id,
                    'total_findings': 0,
                    'total_score': 0,
                    'risk_levels': defaultdict(int),
                    'issue_types': defaultdict(int),
                    'findings': []
                }

            summary[finding.rule_name]['total_findings'] += 1
            summary[finding.rule_name]['total_score'] += finding.score
            summary[finding.rule_name]['risk_levels'][finding.risk_level.value] += 1
            summary[finding.rule_name]['issue_types'][finding.issue_type.value] += 1
            summary[finding.rule_name]['findings'].append({
                'issue_type': finding.issue_type.value,
                'risk_level': finding.risk_level.value,
                'score': finding.score
            })

        return summary
```

```python
    def _generate_remote_management_section(self, results):
        """List ALL remote-management protocols and how many rules allow each."""
        from ..core.models import RuleIssueType

        # Canonical protocols we display (no duplicates)
        ALL_PROTOCOLS = [
            "SSH", "Telnet", "RDP", "VNC", "WinRM (HTTP)", "WinRM (HTTPS)",
            "RSH", "rlogin", "rexec", "XDMCP", "X11", "Apple Remote Desktop",
            "TeamViewer", "AnyDesk", "LogMeIn", "GoToMyPC", "Splashtop",
            "BeyondTrust", "pcAnywhere", "Radmin",
        ]

        # Map any alias/case the checker might emit -> canonical display name
        ALIAS_TO_CANONICAL = {
            "ssh": "SSH", "telnet": "Telnet",
            "rdp": "RDP", "ms-rdp": "RDP", "ms.rdp": "RDP",
            "vnc": "VNC", "vnc-base": "VNC",
            "winrm": "WinRM (HTTP)", "winrm (http)": "WinRM (HTTP)",
            "winrm (https)": "WinRM (HTTPS)",
            "rsh": "RSH", "rlogin": "rlogin", "rexec": "rexec",
            "xdmcp": "XDMCP", "x11": "X11",
            "apple remote desktop": "Apple Remote Desktop",
            "teamviewer": "TeamViewer", "anydesk": "AnyDesk", "logmein": "LogMeIn",
            "gotomypc": "GoToMyPC", "splashtop": "Splashtop",
            "beyondtrust": "BeyondTrust", "pcanywhere": "pcAnywhere", "radmin": "Radmin",
        }

        rm = [f for f in results['findings']
              if f.issue_type == RuleIssueType.MANAGEMENT_ACCESS]

        # Count rules per protocol -- normalize every value to its canonical name
        counts = {}
        for f in rm:
            for p in (f.details or {}).get("protocols", []):
                canonical = ALIAS_TO_CANONICAL.get(str(p).strip().lower(), str(p))
                counts[canonical] = counts.get(canonical, 0) + 1

        found_rows = ""
        notfound_rows = ""
        found_total = 0
        for proto in ALL_PROTOCOLS:
            n = counts.get(proto, 0)
            if n > 0:
                found_total += 1
                found_rows += f"""
                <tr>
                    <td style="font-weight:600;">{proto}</td>
                    <td><span class="risk-badge risk-critical">FOUND</span></td>
                    <td><strong style="color:{self.colors['signature_orange']};">{n}</strong></td>
                </tr>"""
            else:
                notfound_rows += f"""
                <tr style="opacity:0.6;">
                    <td>{proto}</td>
                    <td><span class="risk-badge risk-low">NONE</span></td>
                    <td>0</td>
                </tr>"""

        return f"""
        <div class="section">
            <h2>🖥️ Remote Management Exposure</h2>
            <p style="margin-bottom:20px; color:{self.colors['medium_grey']};">
                List of remote-management protocols and how many rules allow each.
                <strong>{found_total}</strong> protocol(s) found across <strong>{len(rm)}</strong> rule(s).
            </p>
            <table>
                <thead>
                    <tr>
                        <th>Remote Management Protocol</th>
                        <th>Status</th>
                        <th>Rules Allowing It</th>
                    </tr>
                </thead>
                <tbody>
                    {found_rows}
                    {notfound_rows}
                </tbody>
            </table>
        </div>
        """

    def _generate_zone_based_analysis(self, zone_summary: Dict, results: Dict) -> str:
        """Generate zone-based traffic analysis section"""
        if not zone_summary:
            return ""

        zone_pairs_html = ""
        for pair, data in sorted(zone_summary.items(), key=lambda x: x[1]['total_rules'], reverse=True):
            zone_pairs_html += f"""
            <div class="zone-pair-card">
                <div style="font-weight: 600; font-size: 1.1em; margin-bottom: 10px;">{pair}</div>
                <div class="zone-stats">
                    <span class="zone-stat-badge allow">ALLOW: {data['allow_rules']}</span>
                    <span class="zone-stat-badge deny">DENY: {data['deny_rules']}</span>
                    <span class="zone-stat-badge total">TOTAL: {data['total_rules']}</span>
                </div>
            </div>
            """

        return f"""
        <div class="section">
            <h2>🌐 Zone-Based Traffic Analysis</h2>
            <p style="margin-bottom: 20px;">Analysis of traffic flows between configured network zones:</p>
            <div class="zone-pairs-grid">

    def _generate_logging_audit_section(self, results):
        """Logging audit: enabled vs not, and lists of not-logged Allow/Deny rules."""
        from ..core.models import RuleIssueType
        from ..analysis.logging_audit_checker import _logging_enabled

        all_rules = results.get('all_rules') or results.get('rules', [])

        checked = [r for r in all_rules if _logging_enabled(r) is not None]
        if not checked:
            return ""

        enabled_count = sum(1 for r in checked if _logging_enabled(r))
        not_enabled = [r for r in checked if not _logging_enabled(r)]
        no_log_allow = [r for r in not_enabled if r.action.lower() == "allow"]
        no_log_deny = [r for r in not_enabled if r.action.lower() == "deny"]

        def rows(rule_list, badge):
            html = ""
            for r in rule_list:
                html += f"""
                <tr>
                    <td>{r.id}</td>
                    <td style="font-weight:600;">{r.name}</td>
                    <td><span class="action-badge {r.action.lower()}">{r.action.upper()}</span></td>
                    <td><span class="risk-badge {badge}">NO LOGGING</span></td>
                </tr>"""
            return html or '<tr><td colspan="4" style="color:#888;">None</td></tr>'

        return f"""
        <div class="section">
            <h2>📝 Logging Configuration Audit</h2>
            <p style="margin-bottom:20px; color:{self.colors['medium_grey']};">
                Checks whether rules have logging enabled for auditability.
            </p>
            <div class="stats-grid">
                <div class="stat-card">
                    <div class="stat-number">{enabled_count}</div>
                    <div class="stat-label">Logging Enabled</div>
                </div>
                <div class="stat-card">
                    <div class="stat-number">{len(not_enabled)}</div>
                    <div class="stat-label">No Logging</div>
                </div>
                <div class="stat-card">
                    <div class="stat-number">{len(no_log_allow)}</div>
                    <div class="stat-label">No Log + Allow (Critical)</div>
                </div>
                <div class="stat-card">
                    <div class="stat-number">{len(no_log_deny)}</div>
                    <div class="stat-label">No Log + Deny (High)</div>
                </div>
            </div>
            <h3 style="margin-top:30px;">🔴 Allow Rules Without Logging (Critical)</h3>
            <table>
                <thead><tr><th>ID</th><th>Rule Name</th><th>Action</th><th>Status</th></tr></thead>
                <tbody>{rows(no_log_allow, "risk-critical")}</tbody>
            </table>
            <h3 style="margin-top:30px;">🟠 Deny Rules Without Logging (High)</h3>
            <table>
                <thead><tr><th>ID</th><th>Rule Name</th><th>Action</th><th>Status</th></tr></thead>
                <tbody>{rows(no_log_deny, "risk-high")}</tbody>
            </table>
        </div>
        """

    def _generate_zone_traffic_matrix(self, zone_summary: Dict) -> str:
        """Generate zone traffic matrix visualization"""
        if not zone_summary or len(zone_summary) < 2:
            return ""

        zones = set()
        for pair in zone_summary.keys():
            src, dst = pair.split(' → ')
            zones.add(src)
            zones.add(dst)

        zones = sorted(zones)

        matrix_data = {}
        for zone in zones:
            matrix_data[zone] = {}
            for zone2 in zones:
                pair = f"{zone} → {zone2}"
                if pair in zone_summary:
                    matrix_data[zone][zone2] = zone_summary[pair]['total_rules']
                else:
                    matrix_data[zone][zone2] = 0

        matrix_html = "<table class='zone-matrix'><thead><tr><th>From \\ To</th>"
        for zone in zones:
            matrix_html += f"<th>{zone}</th>"
        matrix_html += "</tr></thead><tbody>"

        for src_zone in zones:
            matrix_html += f"<tr><th>{src_zone}</th>"
            for dst_zone in zones:
                count = matrix_data[src_zone][dst_zone]
                color_class = "high" if count > 10 else "medium" if count > 0 else "low"
                matrix_html += f"<td class='matrix-cell {color_class}'>{count}</td>"
            matrix_html += "</tr>"

        matrix_html += "</tbody></table>"

        return f"""
        <div class="section">
            <h2>📊 Zone Traffic Matrix</h2>
            <p style="margin-bottom: 20px;">Number of rules for each source → destination zone pair:</p>
            {matrix_html}
        </div>
        """

    def _evaluate_malicious_ip(self, results):
        rules = results.get('all_rules') or results.get('rules', [])
        critical_rules, deny_rules = [], []
        for rule in rules:
            refs = []
            for v in list(rule.source_addresses) + list(rule.dest_addresses):
                vl = str(v).lower()
                for mal in MALICIOUS_IP_LISTS:
                    if mal.lower() in vl:
                        refs.append(mal)
            refs = sorted(set(refs))
            if not refs:
                continue
            if rule.action.lower() == 'allow':
                critical_rules.append((rule, refs))
            elif rule.action.lower() == 'deny':
                deny_rules.append((rule, refs))
        if critical_rules:
            verdict = 'critical'
        elif deny_rules:
            verdict = 'approved'
        else:
            verdict = 'missing'
        return verdict, critical_rules, deny_rules

    def _generate_malicious_recommendation_box(self, results=None):
        # Detect vendor from the rules
        rules = (results or {}).get('all_rules') or (results or {}).get('rules', [])
        vendor = rules[0].vendor_type.value if rules else "generic"

        # Vendor-specific malicious IP references
        PALO_ALTO_LISTS = [
            "panw-bulletproof-ip-list", "panw-highrisk-ip-list",
            "panw-known-ip-list", "panw-torexit-ip-list",
        ]
        FORTINET_LISTS = [
            "Botnet-C&C.Server", "Malicious-Malicious.Server", "Phishing-Phishing.Server",
            "Spam-Spamming.Server", "Proxy-Proxy.Server", "Tor-Exit.Node",
            "Tor-Relay.Node", "Tor-Tor.Node", "VPN-Anonymous.VPN",
            "Blockchain-Crypto.Mining.Pool",
        ]

        if vendor == "fortinet":
            lists = FORTINET_LISTS
            label = "FortiGate FortiGuard IP Reputation (ISDB) objects"
        elif vendor == "palo_alto":
            lists = PALO_ALTO_LISTS
            label = "Palo Alto built-in malicious IP lists"
        else:
            lists = PALO_ALTO_LISTS + FORTINET_LISTS
            label = "known malicious IP lists / threat feeds"

        items = "".join(f"<li>{m}</li>" for m in lists)
        return f"""
        <div class="critical-alert" style="border-color: {self.colors['warning']};
             background: linear-gradient(135deg, #FFF8E1 0%, {self.colors['white']} 100%);">
            <h3 style="color: {self.colors['warning']};">⚠️ Recommended: Add Malicious IP Blocking</h3>
            <p style="font-size: 1.1em;">No rule was found that blocks the {label}.</p>

    def _generate_complete_findings_table(self, findings: List[SecurityFinding]) -> str:
        """Generate complete findings table with all findings"""
        if not findings:
            return ""

        findings_by_risk = {}
        for finding in findings:
            if finding.risk_level not in findings_by_risk:
                findings_by_risk[finding.risk_level] = []
            findings_by_risk[finding.risk_level].append(finding)

        risk_order = [RiskLevel.CRITICAL, RiskLevel.HIGH, RiskLevel.MEDIUM, RiskLevel.LOW, RiskLevel.INFO]

        html = f"""
        <div class="section">
            <h2>🔍 Complete Security Findings ({len(findings)} Total)</h2>
        """

        for risk_level in risk_order:
            if risk_level not in findings_by_risk:
                continue

            risk_findings = sorted(findings_by_risk[risk_level], key=lambda f: f.score, reverse=True)
            risk_class = f"risk-{risk_level.value}"

            table_id = f"findingsTable_{risk_level.value}"
            rows = ""

            for finding in risk_findings:
                rows += f"""
                <tr>
                    <td>{finding.rule_id}</td>
                    <td>{finding.rule_name}</td>
                    <td>{finding.issue_type.value.replace('_', ' ').title()}</td>
                    <td>{finding.description}</td>
                    <td><strong style="color: {self.colors['signature_orange']};">{finding.score}</strong></td>
                    <td>{finding.calculation_formula[:80]}...</td>
                </tr>
                """

            html += f"""
            <h3 style="margin-top: 30px;">
                <span class="risk-badge {risk_class}">{risk_level.value.upper()}</span>
                Risk Findings ({len(risk_findings)} items)
            </h3>
            <table id="{table_id}" class="findings-datatable">
                <thead>
                    <tr>
                        <th>Rule ID</th>
                        <th>Rule Name</th>
                        <th>Issue Type</th>
                        <th>Description</th>
                        <th>Score</th>
                        <th>Formula</th>
                    </tr>
                </thead>
                <tbody>
                    {rows}
                </tbody>
            </table>
            """

        html += "</div>"
        return html
```
