```python
    def _generate_expired_rules_table(self, findings):
        """Generate table of expired rules (only from ExpiredRuleAnalyzer)."""
        expired = [f for f in findings if f.issue_type.value == 'expired']

        if not expired:
            return ""

        seen = set()
        unique_expired = []
        for f in expired:
            # Only include OUR analyzer's findings (they have 'days_passed')
            if 'days_passed' not in f.details:
                continue

            date = f.details.get('expiry_date')

            # Skip if no valid date
            if not date or str(date).strip() in ('', '-', 'N/A', 'None'):
                continue

            # Skip duplicates
            if f.rule_id in seen:
                continue

            seen.add(f.rule_id)
            unique_expired.append(f)

        if not unique_expired:
            return ""

        rows = ""
        for f in sorted(unique_expired, key=lambda x: x.details.get('days_passed', 0), reverse=True):
            days = f.details.get('days_passed', 'N/A')
            date = f.details.get('expiry_date', 'N/A')
            rows += f"""
            <tr>
                <td>{f.rule_id}</td>
                <td>{f.rule_name}</td>
                <td>{date}</td>
                <td>{days}</td>
                <td>{f.recommendation}</td>
            </tr>
            """

        return f"""
        <div class="section" style="border-left: 6px solid {self.colors['risk_medium']};">
            <h2>⏰ Expired / Temporary Rules ({len(unique_expired)} Total)</h2>
            <p style="margin-bottom: 20px; color: {self.colors['medium_grey']};">
                Time-bound rules whose date has already passed. These should be reviewed, renewed, or removed.
            </p>
            <table>
                <thead>
                    <tr>
                        <th>Rule ID</th>
                        <th>Rule Name</th>
                        <th>Expired Date</th>
                        <th>Days Passed</th>
                        <th>Recommendation</th>
                    </tr>
                </thead>
                <tbody>
                    {rows}
                </tbody>
            </table>
        </div>
        """

    def _generate_security_profile_table(self, findings):
        """Generate table of rules WITH security profiles (deduplicated)."""
        profile_findings = [
            f for f in findings
            if 'HASPROFILE' in f.description
        ]

        if not profile_findings:
            return ""

        # Deduplicate by rule_id
        seen = set()
        unique = []
        for f in profile_findings:
            if f.rule_id not in seen:
                seen.add(f.rule_id)
                unique.append(f)

        rows = ""
        for f in unique:
            profile = f.details.get('security_profile', '')
            rows += f"""
            <tr>
                <td>{f.rule_id}</td>
                <td>{f.rule_name}</td>
                <td style="color: {self.colors['risk_low']}; font-weight: 600;">{profile}</td>
                <td>{f.recommendation}</td>
            </tr>
            """

        return f"""
        <div class="section" style="background: linear-gradient(135deg, #E8F5E9 0%, {self.colors['white']} 100%); border-left: 6px solid {self.colors['risk_low']};">
            <h2>🛡️ Rules With Security Profiles ({len(unique)} Total)</h2>
            <p style="margin-bottom: 20px; color: {self.colors['medium_grey']};">
                ALLOW rules that have security profiles applied (threat inspection enabled). These are correctly protected.
            </p>
            <table>
                <thead>
                    <tr>
                        <th>Rule ID</th>
                        <th>Rule Name</th>
                        <th>Security Profiles</th>
                        <th>Status</th>
                    </tr>
                </thead>
                <tbody>
                    {rows}
                </tbody>
            </table>
        </div>
        """

    
    def _generate_disabled_rules_table(self, disabled_rules: List[FirewallRule]) -> str:
        """Generate table of disabled rules"""
        if not disabled_rules:
            return ""

        rows = ""
        for rule in sorted(disabled_rules, key=lambda r: r.name)[:100]:
            rows += f"""
            <tr>
                <td>{rule.id}</td>
                <td>{rule.name}</td>
                <td>{rule.vendor_type.value.replace('_', ' ').title()}</td>
                <td>{rule.action}</td>
                <td>{len(rule.source_addresses)} sources</td>
                <td>{len(rule.dest_addresses)} destinations</td>
            </tr>
            """

        return f"""
        <div class="section">
            <h2>⊘ Disabled Rules ({len(disabled_rules)} Total)</h2>
            <p style="margin-bottom: 20px; color: {self.colors['medium_grey']};">
                These rules are disabled and not included in active security analysis.
            </p>
            <table>
                <thead>
                    <tr>
                        <th>Rule ID</th>
                        <th>Name</th>
                        <th>Vendor</th>
                        <th>Action</th>
                        <th>Sources</th>
                        <th>Destinations</th>
                    </tr>
                </thead>
                <tbody>
                    {rows}
                </tbody>
            </table>
        </div>
        """

    def _generate_deny_rules_table(self, deny_rules: List[FirewallRule]) -> str:
        """Generate table of DENY rules"""
        if not deny_rules:
            return ""

        deny_rules_filtered = [r for r in deny_rules if not all(
            addr.lower() == 'any' for addr in r.source_addresses + r.dest_addresses
        )]

        if not deny_rules_filtered:
            return ""

        rows = ""
        for rule in sorted(deny_rules_filtered, key=lambda r: r.name)[:50]:
            src_display = ', '.join(rule.source_addresses[:2]) + ('...' if len(rule.source_addresses) > 2 else '')
            dst_display = ', '.join(rule.dest_addresses[:2]) + ('...' if len(rule.dest_addresses) > 2 else '')

            rows += f"""
            <tr>
                <td>{rule.id}</td>
                <td>{rule.name}</td>
                <td>{src_display}</td>
                <td>{dst_display}</td>
                <td>{', '.join(rule.services[:2]) + ('...' if len(rule.services) > 2 else '')}</td>
            </tr>
            """

        return f"""
        <div class="section">
            <h2>🚫 DENY Rules ({len(deny_rules_filtered)} Total)</h2>
            <p style="margin-bottom: 20px; color: {self.colors['medium_grey']};">
                Non-trivial DENY rules shown for reference. Catch-all deny any rules are excluded.
            </p>
            <table>
                <thead>
                    <tr>
                        <th>Rule ID</th>
                        <th>Name</th>
                        <th>Source</th>
                        <th>Destination</th>
                        <th>Service</th>
                    </tr>
                </thead>
                <tbody>
                    {rows}
                </tbody>
            </table>
        </div>
        """
    

    def _generate_full_rule_details_section(self, rules: List[FirewallRule]) -> str:
        """Generate comprehensive section with expandable rule details"""
        if not rules:
            return ""

        # Sort rules by risk score (descending - highest risk first)
        sorted_rules = sorted(rules, key=lambda r: r.risk_score, reverse=True)

        rules_html = ""
        for rule_idx, rule in enumerate(sorted_rules):
            src_tags = self._format_address_list(rule.source_addresses)
            dst_tags = self._format_address_list(rule.dest_addresses)
            svc_tags = self._format_service_list(rule.services)

            action_class = 'allow' if rule.action.lower() == 'allow' else 'deny'

            # Generate findings for this rule
            findings_html = self._format_rule_findings(rule.findings)

            # Risk score color coding
            if rule.risk_score >= 90:
                risk_color = self.colors['risk_critical']
                risk_indicator = '🔴'
            elif rule.risk_score >= 70:
                risk_color = self.colors['risk_high']
                risk_indicator = '🟠'
            elif rule.risk_score >= 40:
                risk_color = self.colors['risk_medium']
                risk_indicator = '🟡'
            elif rule.risk_score >= 20:
                risk_color = self.colors['risk_low']
                risk_indicator = '🟢'
            else:
                risk_color = self.colors['risk_info']
                risk_indicator = '🔵'

            rules_html += f"""
            <div class="rule-detail-section" id="rule-{rule_idx}">
                <div class="rule-detail-header" onclick="toggleRuleDetails({rule_idx})">
                    <div>
                        <h4 style="margin: 0;">
                            <span style="font-size: 1.4em; margin-right: 8px;">{risk_indicator}</span>
                            Rule ID: {rule.id} - {rule.name}
                        </h4>
                        <span style="color: {self.colors['medium_grey']}; font-size: 0.9em;">Click to expand/collapse details</span>
                    </div>
                    <div style="text-align: right;">
                        <span class="action-badge {action_class}">{rule.action.upper()}</span>
                        <span style="margin-left: 10px; font-weight: 600; color: {risk_color}; font-size: 1.1em;">Risk Score: {rule.risk_score}</span>
                    </div>
                </div>

                <div id="rule-details-{rule_idx}" class="collapsed" style="margin-top: 20px;">
                    <div class="rule-detail-body">
                        <div class="detail-group">
                            <h5>Basic Information</h5>
                            <div class="detail-item">
                                <span class="detail-label">Rule ID:</span>
                                <span class="detail-value">{rule.id}</span>
                            </div>
                            <div class="detail-item">
                                <span class="detail-label">Rule Name:</span>
                                <span class="detail-value">{rule.name}</span>
                            </div>
                            <div class="detail-item">
                                <span class="detail-label">Vendor:</span>
                                <span class="detail-value">{rule.vendor_type.value.replace('_', ' ').title()}</span>
                            </div>
                            <div class="detail-item">
                                <span class="detail-label">Action:</span>
                                <span class="detail-value"><span class="action-badge {action_class}">{rule.action.upper()}</span></span>
                            </div>
                            <div class="detail-item">
                                <span class="detail-label">Disabled:</span>
                                <span class="detail-value">{'Yes' if rule.disabled else 'No'}</span>
                            </div>
                            <div class="detail-item">
                                <span class="detail-label">Risk Score:</span>
                                <span class="detail-value" style="font-weight: 700; color: {risk_color}; font-size: 1.05em;">{rule.risk_score}</span>
                            </div>
                        </div>

                        <div class="detail-group">
                            <h5>Zone Configuration</h5>
                            <div class="detail-item">
                                <span class="detail-label">Source Zones:</span>
                                <span class="detail-value">{', '.join(rule.source_zones) if rule.source_zones else 'N/A'}</span>
                            </div>
                            <div class="detail-item">
                                <span class="detail-label">Destination Zones:</span>
                                <span class="detail-value">{', '.join(rule.dest_zones) if rule.dest_zones else 'N/A'}</span>
                            </div>
                            <div class="detail-item">
                                <span class="detail-label">Rule Usage:</span>
                                <span class="detail-value">{rule.rule_usage or 'N/A'}</span>
                            </div>
                            <div class="detail-item">
                                <span class="detail-label">Modified:</span>
                                <span class="detail-value">{rule.modified or 'N/A'}</span>
                            </div>
                        </div>

                        <div class="detail-group" style="grid-column: 1 / -1;">
                            <h5>Source Addresses ({len(rule.source_addresses)})</h5>
                            <div class="detail-value" style="margin-top: 8px;">
                                {src_tags}
                            </div>
                        </div>

                        <div class="detail-group" style="grid-column: 1 / -1;">
                            <h5>Destination Addresses ({len(rule.dest_addresses)})</h5>
                            <div class="detail-value" style="margin-top: 8px;">
                                {dst_tags}
                            </div>
                        </div>

                        <div class="detail-group" style="grid-column: 1 / -1;">
                            <h5>Services ({len(rule.services)})</h5>
                            <div class="detail-value" style="margin-top: 8px;">
                                {svc_tags}
                            </div>
                        </div>

                        <div class="detail-group" style="grid-column: 1 / -1;">
                            <h5>Applications</h5>
                            <div class="detail-value">
                                {', '.join(rule.applications) if rule.applications else 'N/A'}
                            </div>
                        </div>

                        <div class="detail-group" style="grid-column: 1 / -1;">
                            <h5>Source Users</h5>
                            <div class="detail-value">
                                {', '.join(rule.source_users) if rule.source_users else 'N/A'}
                            </div>
                        </div>

                        {findings_html}
                    </div>
                </div>
            </div>
            """

        return f"""
        <div class="section">
            <h2>📋 Complete Rule Details (All {len(rules)} Active Rules - Sorted by Risk Score)</h2>
            <div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 25px;">
                <div style="display: flex; gap: 20px; flex-wrap: wrap;">
                    <div style="display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px;">
                        <span style="font-size: 1.4em;">🔴</span>
                        <span>Critical (≥90)</span>
                    </div>
                    <div style="display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px;">
                        <span style="font-size: 1.4em;">🟠</span>
                        <span>High (70-89)</span>
                    </div>
                    <div style="display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px;">
                        <span style="font-size: 1.4em;">🟡</span>
                        <span>Medium (40-69)</span>
                    </div>
                    <div style="display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px;">
                        <span style="font-size: 1.4em;">🟢</span>
                        <span>Low (20-39)</span>
                    </div>
                    <div style="display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px;">
                        <span style="font-size: 1.4em;">🔵</span>
                        <span>Info (<20)</span>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div style="text-align: right;">
                    <button onclick="toggleAllRules()" style="padding: 10px 20px; background: {self.colors['signature_orange']}; color: {self.colors['white']}; border: none; border-radius: 6px; cursor: pointer; font-weight: 600;">
                        Expand/Collapse All
                    </button>
                </div>
            </div>
            <p style="margin-bottom: 20px; color: {self.colors['medium_grey']};">Click on any rule to expand and view all details. Rules are sorted by risk score (highest first)</p>
            {rules_html}
        </div>
        """

    def _format_address_list(self, addresses: List[str]) -> str:
        """Format address list with styling"""
        html = ""
        for addr in addresses:
            if addr.lower() == 'any':
                html += f"<span class='address-tag any'>ANY</span>"
            elif '/' in addr:
                html += f"<span class='address-tag subnet'>{addr}</span>"
            else:
                html += f"<span class='address-tag ip'>{addr}</span>"
        return html

    def _format_service_list(self, services: List[str]) -> str:
        """Format service list with styling"""
        html = ""
        for svc in services:
            if svc.lower() == 'any':
                html += f"<span class='service-tag any'>ANY</span>"
            else:
                html += f"<span class='service-tag'>{svc}</span>"
        return html

    def _format_rule_findings(self, findings: List[SecurityFinding]) -> str:
        """Format findings for rule detail view"""
        if not findings:
            return f"""
            <div class="detail-group" style="grid-column: 1 / -1; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #C8E6C9 0%, {self.colors['white']} 100%);">
                <h5>Security Findings</h5>
                <div style="color: {self.colors['risk_low']}; font-weight: 600;">✓ No security findings for this rule</div>
            </div>
            """

        html = f"""
        <div class="detail-group" style="grid-column: 1 / -1;">
            <h5>Security Findings ({len(findings)})</h5>
        """

        for finding in findings:
            html += f"""
            <div style="background: {self.colors['white']}; padding: 15px; border-radius: 8px; margin-top: 12px; border-left: 5px solid var(--risk-{finding.risk_level.value}, {self.colors['risk_' + finding.risk_level.value]});">
                <div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: start; margin-bottom: 10px;">
                    <span class="risk-badge risk-{finding.risk_level.value}">{finding.risk_level.value.upper()}</span>
                    <span style="font-weight: 600; color: {self.colors['signature_orange']};">Score: {finding.score}</span>
                </div>
                <div style="font-weight: 600; margin-bottom: 8px;">{finding.issue_type.value.replace('_', ' ').title()}</div>
                <div style="color: {self.colors['medium_grey']}; margin-bottom: 8px;">{finding.description}</div>
                <div style="background: {self.colors['very_light_grey']}; padding: 10px; border-radius: 6px; font-size: 0.95em;">
                    <strong>Recommendation:</strong> {finding.recommendation}
                </div>
                <div style="background: {self.colors['dark_grey']}; color: {self.colors['white']}; padding: 10px; border-radius: 6px; font-size: 0.85em; margin-top: 10px; font-family: monospace; overflow-x: auto;">
                    <strong>Calculation:</strong> {finding.calculation_formula}
                </div>
            </div>
            """

        html += "</div>"
        return html

    def _generate_footer(self) -> str:
        """Generate footer"""
        return f"""
        <footer>
            <p><strong>Multi-Vendor Firewall Security Analysis Report</strong></p>
            <p>Enhanced Security Analyzer - Full Implementation with All Features</p>
            <p style="margin-top: 12px; opacity: 0.9;">Zone-Based Analysis • Subnet Overlap Detection • Complete Rule Visibility • Comprehensive Risk Scoring</p>
            <p style="margin-top: 8px; opacity: 0.8;">Report generated on {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d at %H:%M:%S')}</p>
        </footer>
        """
```

```css
/* Firewall Analyzer report stylesheet.

 */

body {
```

## `src/firewall_analyzer/reporting/assets/report.js`

```javascript
/* Firewall Analyzer report behaviour.
 * Reads render-time data from the global REPORT_CONFIG object, which
 * _get_enhanced_javascript() emits immediately before this file.
 */
// ==========================================================
// Existing rule details
// ==========================================================

var allRulesExpanded = false;

// ==========================================================
// External Communications Discovery
// ==========================================================

var externalZones = [];
var externalDiscoveryResults = [];
var portAnalysisResults = [];

function analyzeExternalPorts() {

    if (externalDiscoveryResults.length === 0) {
        alert("Run External Discovery first.");
        return;
    }

    let portCounts = {};

    externalDiscoveryResults.forEach(function(rule) {

        let services = rule.services || [];

        services.forEach(function(service) {

            service.split(";").forEach(function(item) {

                if (
                    item.toLowerCase().startsWith("g_")
                ) {
                    return;
                }

                if (
                    !item ||
                    item.toLowerCase() === "any" ||
                    item.toLowerCase() === "application-default"
                ) {
                    return;
                }

                if (!portCounts[item]) {
                    portCounts[item] = 0;
                }

                portCounts[item]++;
            });
        });
    });

    portAnalysisResults =
        Object.entries(portCounts)
            .sort(function(a, b) {
                return b[1] - a[1];
            });

    let html = `
        <h3>External Ports</h3>

        <table>
            <tr>
                <th>Port / Service</th>
                <th>Rules</th>
            </tr>
    `;

    portAnalysisResults.forEach(function(row) {

        html += `
            <tr>
                <td>${row[0]}</td>
                <td>${row[1]}</td>
            </tr>
        `;
    });

    html += "</table>";

    document.getElementById(
        "externalPortsTable"
    ).innerHTML = html;
}

function findInsecurePorts() {

    if (externalDiscoveryResults.length === 0) {

        alert(
            "Run External Discovery first."
        );

        return;
    }

    const insecurePorts = {
        "20": "FTP Data",
        "21": "FTP",
        "23": "Telnet",
        "25": "SMTP",
        "53": "DNS",
        "69": "TFTP",
        "80": "HTTP",
        "110": "POP3",
        "111": "RPC",
        "135": "Microsoft RPC",
        "137": "NetBIOS Name Service",
        "138": "NetBIOS Datagram",
        "139": "NetBIOS Session",
        "143": "IMAP",
        "161": "SNMP",
        "162": "SNMP Trap",
        "389": "LDAP",
        "445": "SMB",
        "2049": "NFS",
        "3389": "RDP",
        "5900": "VNC"
    };

    let findings = [];

    externalDiscoveryResults.forEach(function(rule) {

        let services = rule.services || [];

        services.forEach(function(service) {

            Object.keys(
                insecurePorts
            ).forEach(function(port) {

                var portRegex = new RegExp(
                    "(^|[^0-9])" + port + "([^0-9]|$)"
                );

                if (
                    portRegex.test(
                        service.toLowerCase()
                    )
                ) {

                    findings.push({
                        rule: rule.name,
                        service: service,
                        risk: insecurePorts[port]
                    });
                }
            });
        });
    });

    let html = `
        <h3>
            Potentially Insecure Ports
        </h3>

        <table>
            <tr>
                <th>Rule</th>
                <th>Service</th>
                <th>Risk</th>
            </tr>
    `;

    findings.forEach(function(item) {

        html += `
            <tr>
                <td>${item.rule}</td>
                <td>${item.service}</td>
                <td>${item.risk}</td>
            </tr>
        `;
    });

    html += "</table>";

    document.getElementById(
        "insecurePortsTable"
    ).innerHTML = html;
}




function normalizeZone(zone) {
    return String(zone || "")
        .replace("[Disabled]", "")
        .trim()
        .toLowerCase();
}

function escapeHtml(value) {
    return String(value || "")
        .replace(/&/g, "&amp;")
        .replace(/</g, "&lt;")
        .replace(/>/g, "&gt;")
        .replace(/"/g, "&quot;")
        .replace(/'/g, "&#039;");
}

function addExternalZone() {
    var input = document.getElementById("externalZoneInput");

    if (!input) {
        return;
    }

    var zone = input.value.trim();

    if (!zone) {
        return;
    }

    var alreadyExists = externalZones.some(function(existingZone) {
        return normalizeZone(existingZone) === normalizeZone(zone);
    });

    if (!alreadyExists) {
        externalZones.push(zone);
    }

    renderExternalZones();
    input.value = "";
}

function removeExternalZone(index) {
    externalZones.splice(index, 1);
    renderExternalZones();
}

function renderExternalZones() {
    var container = document.getElementById("externalZonesList");

    if (!container) {
        return;
    }

    var html = "";

    externalZones.forEach(function(zone, index) {
        html += `
            <span style="
                background:#EB8C00;
                color:white;
                padding:8px 12px;
                margin:5px;
                display:inline-block;
                border-radius:6px;
                font-weight:bold;
            ">
                ${escapeHtml(zone)}

                <button
                    type="button"
                    onclick="removeExternalZone(${index})"
                    style="
                        margin-left:8px;
                        padding:0;
                        background:transparent;
                        color:white;
                        border:none;
                        cursor:pointer;
                        font-size:16px;
                        font-weight:bold;
                    "
                    title="Remove zone"
                >
                    ×
                </button>
            </span>
        `;
    });

    container.innerHTML = html;
}

function runExternalDiscovery() {
    if (externalZones.length === 0) {
        alert("Please add at least one external zone.");
        return;
    }

    var rules = window.externalDiscoveryRules || [];

    if (rules.length === 0) {
        alert("No firewall rules are available in the report.");
        return;
    }

    var normalizedExternalZones = externalZones.map(normalizeZone);

    var activeAllowRules = rules.filter(function(rule) {

    var action = String(rule.action || "")
        .trim()
        .toLowerCase();

    var sourceZones = rule.source_zones || [];
    var destinationZones = rule.destination_zones || [];

    var disabledInSourceZone = sourceZones.some(function(zone) {
        return String(zone)
            .trim()
            .toLowerCase()
            .includes("[disabled]");
    });

    var disabledInDestinationZone =
        destinationZones.some(function(zone) {
            return String(zone)
                .trim()
                .toLowerCase()
                .includes("[disabled]");
        });

    return (
        !rule.disabled &&
        !action.includes("[disabled]") &&
        !disabledInSourceZone &&
        !disabledInDestinationZone &&
        ["allow", "accept", "permit"].includes(action)
    );
});


    var confirmedExternal = [];
    var potentialExternal = [];
    var internalRules = [];

    activeAllowRules.forEach(function(rule) {
        var sourceZones = (rule.source_zones || []).map(normalizeZone);
        var destinationZones =
            (rule.destination_zones || []).map(normalizeZone);

        var sourceMatch = sourceZones.some(function(zone) {
            return normalizedExternalZones.includes(zone);
        });

        var destinationMatch = destinationZones.some(function(zone) {
            return normalizedExternalZones.includes(zone);
        });

        var sourceAny = sourceZones.includes("any");
        var destinationAny = destinationZones.includes("any");

        var result = Object.assign({}, rule);

        if (sourceMatch || destinationMatch) {
            result.match_type = "Confirmed External";

            var matchedDirections = [];

            if (sourceMatch) {
                matchedDirections.push("Source Zone");
            }

            if (destinationMatch) {
                matchedDirections.push("Destination Zone");
            }

            result.match_reason =
                matchedDirections.join(" and ") +
                " matched an entered external zone";

            confirmedExternal.push(result);

        } else if (sourceAny || destinationAny) {
            result.match_type = "Potential External";

            var anyDirections = [];

            if (sourceAny) {
                anyDirections.push("Source Zone is Any");
            }

            if (destinationAny) {
                anyDirections.push("Destination Zone is Any");
            }

            result.match_reason = anyDirections.join(" and ");

            potentialExternal.push(result);

        } else {
            result.match_type = "Internal";
            result.match_reason =
                "No source or destination zone matched an external zone";

            internalRules.push(result);
        }
    });

    externalDiscoveryResults =
        confirmedExternal.concat(potentialExternal);

    var totalElement =
        document.getElementById("totalAllowRulesCount");

    var confirmedElement =
        document.getElementById("confirmedExternalCount");

    var potentialElement =
        document.getElementById("potentialExternalCount");

    var internalElement =
        document.getElementById("internalRulesCount");

    if (totalElement) {
        totalElement.textContent = activeAllowRules.length;
    }

    if (confirmedElement) {
        confirmedElement.textContent = confirmedExternal.length;
    }

    if (potentialElement) {
        potentialElement.textContent = potentialExternal.length;
    }

    if (internalElement) {
        internalElement.textContent = internalRules.length;
    }

    var messageContainer =
        document.getElementById("externalDiscoveryMessage");

    if (messageContainer) {
        messageContainer.innerHTML = `
            <div style="
                padding:15px;
                background:#F5F5F5;
                border-left:5px solid #EB8C00;
                border-radius:6px;
            ">
                Analysis completed using external zones:
                <strong>
                    ${externalZones.map(escapeHtml).join(", ")}
                </strong>
            </div>
        `;
    }

    renderExternalResultsTable(externalDiscoveryResults);

    var downloadButton =
        document.getElementById("downloadExternalCsvButton");

    if (downloadButton) {
        downloadButton.style.display =
            externalDiscoveryResults.length > 0
                ? "inline-block"
                : "none";
    }
}

function renderExternalResultsTable(results) {
    var container =
        document.getElementById("externalResultsTable");

    if (!container) {
        return;
    }

    if (results.length === 0) {
        container.innerHTML = `
            <div style="
                padding:20px;
                background:#E8F5E9;
                border-left:5px solid #2E7D32;
                border-radius:6px;
            ">
                No external communication rules were found.
            </div>
        `;

        return;
    }

    var rows = "";

    results.forEach(function(rule) {
        var badgeColor =
            rule.match_type === "Confirmed External"
                ? "#F44336"
                : "#FF9800";

        rows += `
            <tr>
                <td>${escapeHtml(rule.id)}</td>

                <td>${escapeHtml(rule.name)}</td>

                <td>
                    ${escapeHtml(
                        (rule.source_zones || []).join("; ")
                    )}
                </td>

                <td>
                    ${escapeHtml(
                        (rule.destination_zones || []).join("; ")
                    )}
                </td>

                <td>
                    ${escapeHtml(
                        (rule.applications || []).join("; ")
                    )}
                </td>

                <td>
                    ${escapeHtml(
                        (rule.services || []).join("; ")
                    )}
                </td>

                <td>${escapeHtml(rule.action)}</td>

                <td>
                    <span style="
                        display:inline-block;
                        padding:5px 10px;
                        border-radius:5px;
                        background:${badgeColor};
                        color:white;
                        font-weight:bold;
                    ">
                        ${escapeHtml(rule.match_type)}
                    </span>
                </td>

                <td>${escapeHtml(rule.match_reason)}</td>
            </tr>
        `;
    });

    container.innerHTML = `
        <h3>
            External Communication Rules
            (${results.length})
        </h3>

        <table>
            <thead>
                <tr>
                    <th>Rule ID</th>
                    <th>Rule Name</th>
                    <th>Source Zones</th>
                    <th>Destination Zones</th>
                    <th>Applications</th>
                    <th>Services</th>
                    <th>Action</th>
                    <th>Match Type</th>
                    <th>Reason</th>
                </tr>
            </thead>

            <tbody>
                ${rows}
            </tbody>
        </table>
    `;
}

function csvSafe(value) {
    var text = String(value || "");
    return '"' + text.replace(/"/g, '""') + '"';
}

function downloadExternalCommunicationsCSV() {
    if (externalDiscoveryResults.length === 0) {
        alert("No external communication results to download.");
        return;
    }

    var csvRows = [];

    csvRows.push([
        "Rule ID",
        "Rule Name",
        "Source Zones",
        "Destination Zones",
        "Source Addresses",
        "Destination Addresses",
        "Applications",
        "Services",
        "Action",
        "Match Type",
        "Match Reason"
    ].map(csvSafe).join(","));

    externalDiscoveryResults.forEach(function(rule) {
        csvRows.push([
            rule.id,
            rule.name,
            (rule.source_zones || []).join("; "),
            (rule.destination_zones || []).join("; "),
            (rule.source_addresses || []).join("; "),
            (rule.destination_addresses || []).join("; "),
            (rule.applications || []).join("; "),
            (rule.services || []).join("; "),
            rule.action,
            rule.match_type,
            rule.match_reason
        ].map(csvSafe).join(","));
    });

    var csvContent = csvRows.join("\\n");

    var blob = new Blob(
        [csvContent],
        { type: "text/csv;charset=utf-8;" }
    );

    var url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
    var link = document.createElement("a");

    link.href = url;
    link.download = "OUTPUT_external_communications.csv";

    document.body.appendChild(link);
    link.click();
    document.body.removeChild(link);

    URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
}

// ==========================================================
// Existing rule details functions
// ==========================================================

function toggleRuleDetails(ruleIdx) {
    var detailsDiv =
        document.getElementById("rule-details-" + ruleIdx);

    if (!detailsDiv) {
        return;
    }

    if (detailsDiv.classList.contains("collapsed")) {
        detailsDiv.classList.remove("collapsed");
        detailsDiv.classList.add("expanded");
    } else {
        detailsDiv.classList.remove("expanded");
        detailsDiv.classList.add("collapsed");
    }
}

function toggleAllRules() {
    var ruleSections =
        document.querySelectorAll('[id^="rule-details-"]');

    allRulesExpanded = !allRulesExpanded;

    ruleSections.forEach(function(section) {
        if (allRulesExpanded) {
            section.classList.remove("collapsed");
            section.classList.add("expanded");
        } else {
            section.classList.remove("expanded");
            section.classList.add("collapsed");
        }
    });
}

// ==========================================================
// Initialize DataTables
// ==========================================================

$(document).ready(function() {
    var tables =
        document.querySelectorAll("table.findings-datatable");

    tables.forEach(function(table) {
        if (!$.fn.DataTable.isDataTable(table)) {
            $(table).DataTable({
                "paging": true,
                "pageLength": 10,
                "searching": true,
                "ordering": true,
                "info": true,
                "autoWidth": false,
                "lengthChange": true,
                "lengthMenu": [
                    [10, 25, 50, 100],
                    [10, 25, 50, 100]
                ],
                "dom": '<"top"lf>rt<"bottom"ip>',
                "language": {
                    "search": "Filter findings:",
                    "lengthMenu": "Show _MENU_ entries",
                    "info":
                        "Showing _START_ to _END_ of _TOTAL_ findings",
                    "paginate": {
```

## `src/firewall_analyzer/utils/ip_utils.py`

```python
import ipaddress
from typing import Tuple, Any, Dict


class IPAddressUtils:
    """Utilities for IP address and subnet operations"""

    @staticmethod
    def parse_ip_or_subnet(address: str) -> Tuple[bool, Any]:
        """
        Parse IP address or subnet notation
        Returns (is_valid, ipaddress_object or None)
        """
        address = address.strip().lower()

        if address in ['any', 'all', '*', '0.0.0.0']:
            return True, None

        try:
            if '/' in address:
                network = ipaddress.ip_network(address, strict=False)
                return True, network
            else:
                ip = ipaddress.ip_address(address)
                return True, ip
        except ValueError:
            return False, None

    @staticmethod
    def subnet_overlap_check(subnet1: str, subnet2: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Check if two subnets overlap
        Returns: {overlaps: bool, overlap_type: str, details: dict}
        """
        valid1, obj1 = IPAddressUtils.parse_ip_or_subnet(subnet1)
        valid2, obj2 = IPAddressUtils.parse_ip_or_subnet(subnet2)

        if not valid1 or not valid2 or obj1 is None or obj2 is None:
            return {'overlaps': False, 'overlap_type': 'invalid', 'details': {}}

        try:
            if isinstance(obj1, ipaddress.IPv4Address):
                net1 = ipaddress.ip_network(obj1, strict=False)
            else:
                net1 = obj1

            if isinstance(obj2, ipaddress.IPv4Address):
                net2 = ipaddress.ip_network(obj2, strict=False)
            else:
                net2 = obj2

            if net1 == net2:
                return {
                    'overlaps': True,
                    'overlap_type': 'identical',
                    'details': {'subnet1': str(net1), 'subnet2': str(net2)}
                }

            if net1.subnet_of(net2):
                return {
                    'overlaps': True,
                    'overlap_type': 'contained_in',
                    'details': {
                        'subnet1': str(net1),
                        'subnet2': str(net2),
                        'relationship': f"{net1} is contained in {net2}"
                    }
                }

            if net2.subnet_of(net1):
                return {
                    'overlaps': True,
                    'overlap_type': 'contains',
                    'details': {
                        'subnet1': str(net1),
                        'subnet2': str(net2),
                        'relationship': f"{net2} is contained in {net1}"
                    }
                }

            if net1.overlaps(net2):
                return {
                    'overlaps': True,
                    'overlap_type': 'partial_overlap',
                    'details': {'subnet1': str(net1), 'subnet2': str(net2)}
                }

            return {'overlaps': False, 'overlap_type': 'no_overlap', 'details': {}}

        except Exception as e:
            return {'overlaps': False, 'overlap_type': 'error', 'details': {'error': str(e)}}

    @staticmethod
    def ip_in_subnet(ip_address: str, subnet: str) -> bool:
        """Check if IP address is within subnet"""
        valid_ip, obj_ip = IPAddressUtils.parse_ip_or_subnet(ip_address)
        valid_subnet, obj_subnet = IPAddressUtils.parse_ip_or_subnet(subnet)

        if not valid_ip or not valid_subnet or obj_ip is None or obj_subnet is None:
            return False

        try:
            if isinstance(obj_ip, ipaddress.IPv4Network):
                obj_ip = obj_ip.network_address

            if isinstance(obj_subnet, ipaddress.IPv4Address):
                obj_subnet = ipaddress.ip_network(obj_subnet, strict=False)

            return obj_ip in obj_subnet
        except Exception:
            return False

    @staticmethod
    def get_subnet_size(subnet: str) -> int:
        """Get number of hosts in subnet"""
        valid, obj = IPAddressUtils.parse_ip_or_subnet(subnet)

        if not valid or obj is None:
            return 0

        try:
            if isinstance(obj, ipaddress.IPv4Address):
                return 1
            else:
                return obj.num_addresses
        except Exception:
            return 0
```

## `src/firewall_analyzer/webui/cli.py`

```python
"""`firewall-analyzer-ui` — start the web interface.

Deliberately one command with working defaults: on a managed device the goal is
that a team member types one thing and gets a browser tab, with no config file,
no container runtime and no shell script.
"""

import argparse
import socket
import sys
import threading
import webbrowser


def _port_is_free(host: str, port: int) -> bool:
    with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as sock:
        sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
        try:
            sock.bind((host, port))
            return True
        except OSError:
            return False


def _pick_port(host: str, preferred: int) -> int:
    """Use the requested port, else the next free one — a second person
    starting the UI should not get a stack trace."""
    for candidate in range(preferred, preferred + 20):
        if _port_is_free(host, candidate):
            return candidate
    raise SystemExit(f"No free port between {preferred} and {preferred + 19}.")


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="firewall-analyzer-ui",
        description="Start the Firewall Analyzer web interface.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1",
                        help="Interface to bind (default: 127.0.0.1, local only). "
                             "Use 0.0.0.0 to share with your team on the network.")
    parser.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=8000, help="Port (default: 8000)")
    parser.add_argument("--no-browser", action="store_true",
                        help="Do not open a browser window")
    parser.add_argument("--reload", action="store_true",
                        help="Reload on code changes (development)")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    try:
        import uvicorn  # noqa: F401
    except ImportError:
        print(
            "The web interface needs a few extra packages. Install them with:\n\n"
            '    pip install "firewall_analyzer[ui]"\n\n'
            "or, from a source checkout:\n\n"
            '    pip install -e ".[ui]"',
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 1

    from . import config

    port = args.port if args.reload else _pick_port(args.host, args.port)
    shown_host = "127.0.0.1" if args.host in ("0.0.0.0", "::") else args.host
    url = f"http://{shown_host}:{port}"

    config.ensure_dirs()
    appid = config.APPID_DB if config.APPID_DB.exists() else "not found (application risk disabled)"
    banner = [
        "",
        "  Firewall Analyzer",
        f"  {url}",
        "",
        f"  data      {config.DATA_DIR}",
        f"  appid db  {appid}",
    ]
    if args.host in ("0.0.0.0", "::"):
        banner += ["", "  Listening on all interfaces - reachable by others on your network."]
    banner += ["", "  Ctrl+C to stop", ""]
    # flush: stdout is block-buffered when this is piped or run as a service,
    # which would otherwise hide the URL until shutdown.
    print("\n".join(banner), flush=True)

    if not args.no_browser:
        threading.Timer(1.2, lambda: webbrowser.open(url)).start()

    import uvicorn
    uvicorn.run(
        "firewall_analyzer.webui.main:app",
        host=args.host,
        port=port,
        reload=args.reload,
        log_level="warning",
    )
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

## `src/firewall_analyzer/webui/config.py`

```python
"""Runtime settings for the Firewall Analyzer web UI.

Every path is environment-overridable, and every default works from an
installed copy as well as a source checkout - the UI is meant to be started
with one command on a locked-down machine, not configured first.
"""

import os
from pathlib import Path

#: The installed package directory (…/firewall_analyzer/webui).
PACKAGE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent

#: The repo root when running from a source checkout; None once installed.
_repo_root = PACKAGE_DIR.parents[2]
REPO_ROOT = _repo_root if (_repo_root / "pyproject.toml").exists() else None

STATIC_DIR = PACKAGE_DIR / "static"


def _env_path(name: str, default: Path) -> Path:
    return Path(os.environ.get(name, default)).expanduser().resolve()


def _default_data_dir() -> Path:
    """Uploads, reports and the database.

    A source checkout keeps them in `var/` beside the code, which is gitignored.
    An installed copy uses a per-user directory so nothing is written next to
    site-packages - that is usually read-only on a managed device.
    """
    if REPO_ROOT:
        return REPO_ROOT / "var"
    return Path.home() / ".firewall-analyzer"


DATA_DIR = _env_path("FWA_DATA_DIR", _default_data_dir())
UPLOAD_DIR = DATA_DIR / "uploads"
REPORT_DIR = DATA_DIR / "reports"
DB_PATH = _env_path("FWA_DB_PATH", DATA_DIR / "firewall_analyzer.db")


def _find_appid_db() -> Path:
    """Locate the Applipedia database.

    It is ~6 MB, so it is not shipped inside the wheel. Known locations are
    tried in turn; the last is returned when none exist, and the handler then
    emits its usual "not found" warning - analyses still run, they just lose
    application-risk enrichment.
    """
    candidates = [
        Path.cwd() / "data" / "palo_alto_applipedia.json",
        Path.cwd() / "palo_alto_applipedia.json",
        DATA_DIR / "palo_alto_applipedia.json",
    ]
    if REPO_ROOT:
        candidates.insert(0, REPO_ROOT / "data" / "palo_alto_applipedia.json")
    for candidate in candidates:
        if candidate.exists():
            return candidate
    return candidates[-1]


APPID_DB = (
    Path(os.environ["FWA_APPID_DB"]).expanduser().resolve()
    if os.environ.get("FWA_APPID_DB")
    else _find_appid_db()
)

#: The full scoring config shipped inside the package. Deliberately NOT the
#: repo-root analysis_config.json, which disables application risk scoring and
#: would silently drop findings from every run.
ANALYSIS_CONFIG = _env_path(
    "FWA_ANALYSIS_CONFIG", PACKAGE_DIR.parent / "config" / "analysis_config.json"
)

#: Uploads larger than this are rejected before anything is written to disk.
MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES = int(os.environ.get("FWA_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES", 64 * 1024 * 1024))

#: Analysis is CPU-bound and single-threaded; a small pool keeps the API
#: responsive without starving it.
MAX_WORKERS = int(os.environ.get("FWA_MAX_WORKERS", 2))


def ensure_dirs() -> None:
    for directory in (DATA_DIR, UPLOAD_DIR, REPORT_DIR):
        directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
```

## `src/firewall_analyzer/webui/jobs.py`

```python
"""Background execution of analyses.

Analysis is CPU-bound and takes seconds to minutes, so it must not run inside
the request. A small thread pool owns the work; the API polls the row for
status. That keeps the deployment to one process - no broker, no worker service
- which suits a tool a team runs against its own exports.
"""

import logging
import traceback
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional

from . import config, store
from .runner import run_analysis

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_pool = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=config.MAX_WORKERS, thread_name_prefix="analysis")


def submit(analysis_id: str, source_path: Path, vendor: Optional[str]) -> None:
    _pool.submit(_execute, analysis_id, source_path, vendor)


def shutdown() -> None:
    _pool.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True)


def _execute(analysis_id: str, source_path: Path, vendor: Optional[str]) -> None:
    report_path = config.REPORT_DIR / f"{analysis_id}.html"

    def progress(step: str) -> None:
        store.update_analysis(analysis_id, progress=step)

    store.update_analysis(
        analysis_id, status="running", started_at=store.now(), progress="Starting"
    )
    try:
        meta, findings, rules = run_analysis(
            source_path, vendor=vendor, report_path=report_path, progress=progress
        )
        store.insert_findings(analysis_id, findings)
        store.insert_rules(analysis_id, rules)
        store.update_analysis(
            analysis_id,
            status="succeeded",
            progress=None,
            finished_at=store.now(),
            vendor=meta["vendor"],
            summary=_json(meta["summary"]),
            stats=_json(meta["stats"]),
            zone_summary=_json(meta["zone_summary"]),
            report_path=str(report_path),
        )
        logger.info("analysis %s succeeded (%d findings)", analysis_id, len(findings))
    except Exception as exc:
        logger.exception("analysis %s failed", analysis_id)
        store.update_analysis(
            analysis_id,
            status="failed",
            progress=None,
            finished_at=store.now(),
            error=f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"[:2000],
        )
        logger.debug("%s", traceback.format_exc())


def _json(value: object) -> str:
    import json

    return json.dumps(value)
```

## `src/firewall_analyzer/webui/main.py`

```python
"""Firewall Analyzer API service entry point.

Serves the JSON API under /api and, when the static bundle is present, the
frontend itself - so `uvicorn app.main:app` is the whole application in
development. In the container split, nginx serves the frontend and proxies
/api here.
"""

import logging
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.responses import FileResponse, JSONResponse
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles

from . import config, jobs, runner, store
from .routers import analyses, meta

logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)-8s %(name)s: %(message)s",
)
logger = logging.getLogger("firewall_analyzer.api")

STATIC_DIR = config.STATIC_DIR


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_app: FastAPI):
    config.ensure_dirs()
    store.init_db()
    logger.info("database ready at %s", config.DB_PATH)
    try:
        runner.warm_up()
    except Exception:
        # A missing Applipedia file must not stop the service; analyses still
        # run, they just lose application risk enrichment.
        logger.warning("Applipedia database unavailable at %s", config.APPID_DB)
    yield
    jobs.shutdown()


app = FastAPI(
    title="Firewall Analyzer API",
    version="1.0.0",
    lifespan=lifespan,
    docs_url="/api/docs",
    openapi_url="/api/openapi.json",
)

app.include_router(analyses.router, prefix="/api")
app.include_router(meta.router, prefix="/api")


@app.exception_handler(Exception)
async def unhandled(request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:
    logger.exception("unhandled error on %s %s", request.method, request.url.path)
    return JSONResponse(
        status_code=500,
        content={"detail": "Internal server error", "error_code": "INTERNAL"},
    )


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- frontend

if STATIC_DIR.is_dir():
    app.mount("/css", StaticFiles(directory=STATIC_DIR / "css"), name="css")
    app.mount("/js", StaticFiles(directory=STATIC_DIR / "js"), name="js")
    app.mount("/img", StaticFiles(directory=STATIC_DIR / "img"), name="img")

    @app.get("/", include_in_schema=False)
    def index():
        return FileResponse(STATIC_DIR / "app.html")

    @app.get("/favicon.ico", include_in_schema=False)
    def favicon():
        icon = STATIC_DIR / "img" / "favicon.svg"
        if icon.exists():
            return FileResponse(icon, media_type="image/svg+xml")
        return JSONResponse(status_code=404, content={"detail": "no favicon"})
```

## `src/firewall_analyzer/webui/runner.py`

```python
"""Bridges the API to the `firewall_analyzer` package.

The analyzer is imported and driven in-process rather than shelled out to, so
results arrive as objects instead of being parsed back out of HTML. Two things
matter for responsiveness:

* The Applipedia database (~6 MB of JSON, 5k applications) is loaded once and
  shared by every run. Parsing it per analysis dominated the CLI's runtime.
* The analyzers print progress to stdout. That output is captured per run rather
  than being allowed to interleave in the server log.
"""

import contextlib
import csv
import io
import json
import logging
import threading
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

from firewall_analyzer.config.manager import ConfigurationManager
from firewall_analyzer.core.models import FirewallRule, SecurityFinding, VendorType
from firewall_analyzer.data.appid_handler import PaloAltoAppIDHandler
from firewall_analyzer.data.parser import MultiVendorCSVParser
from firewall_analyzer.orchestrator import EnhancedFirewallRuleAnalyzer
from firewall_analyzer.reporting.html_generator import EnhancedHTMLReportGenerator

from . import config

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_appid_lock = threading.Lock()
_appid_handler: Optional[PaloAltoAppIDHandler] = None


def get_appid_handler() -> PaloAltoAppIDHandler:
    """Load the Applipedia database once, on first use."""
    global _appid_handler
    with _appid_lock:
        if _appid_handler is None:
            logger.info("loading Applipedia database from %s", config.APPID_DB)
            with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
                _appid_handler = PaloAltoAppIDHandler(str(config.APPID_DB))
            logger.info("Applipedia ready: %d applications", len(_appid_handler.app_id_database))
    return _appid_handler


def warm_up() -> None:
    """Called at startup so the first user request is not the one that pays."""
    get_appid_handler()


# --------------------------------------------------------------- input prep

EXCEL_SUFFIXES = {".xlsx", ".xls", ".xlsm"}


def to_csv(source: Path) -> Path:
    """Return a CSV path for `source`, converting a spreadsheet if needed.

    The analyzer's parser reads CSV only; handing it a .xlsx produces an opaque
    UTF-8 decode error. Converting here means the UI can accept either.
    """
    if source.suffix.lower() not in EXCEL_SUFFIXES:
        return source

    try:
        import openpyxl
    except ImportError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - dependency is declared
        raise RuntimeError(
            "Excel upload needs the 'openpyxl' package on the API service."
        ) from exc

    book = openpyxl.load_workbook(source, read_only=True, data_only=True)
    sheet = book.active
    target = source.with_suffix(".converted.csv")
    with open(target, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        writer = csv.writer(handle)
        for row in sheet.iter_rows(values_only=True):
            writer.writerow(["" if cell is None else cell for cell in row])
    book.close()
    return target


def sniff_headers(source: Path) -> List[str]:
    """Column names of the uploaded file, for the wizard's preview step."""
    path = to_csv(source)
    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as handle:
        reader = csv.reader(handle)
        for row in reader:
            if any(cell.strip() for cell in row):
                return [cell.strip() for cell in row]
    return []


# ------------------------------------------------------------ serialization


def _finding_dict(finding: SecurityFinding) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "rule_id": str(finding.rule_id),
        "rule_name": finding.rule_name,
        "issue_type": finding.issue_type.value,
        "risk_level": finding.risk_level.value,
        "score": int(finding.score),
        "description": finding.description,
        "recommendation": finding.recommendation,
        "formula": finding.calculation_formula or "",
        "details": _jsonable(finding.details),
    }


def _rule_dict(rule: FirewallRule, seq: int) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "seq": seq,
        "rule_id": str(rule.id),
        "name": rule.name,
        "action": (rule.action or "").lower(),
        "disabled": bool(rule.disabled),
        "src_zones": list(rule.source_zones),
        "dst_zones": list(rule.dest_zones),
        "src_addresses": list(rule.source_addresses),
        "dst_addresses": list(rule.dest_addresses),
        "services": list(rule.services),
        "applications": list(rule.applications),
        "logging": rule.logging or "",
        "rule_usage": rule.rule_usage or "",
        "risk_score": int(rule.risk_score),
        "finding_count": len(rule.findings),
        "raw": _jsonable(rule.raw_data),
    }


def _jsonable(value: Any) -> Any:
    """Coerce analyzer payloads into something json.dumps accepts.

    Findings carry `details` dicts assembled ad hoc by each analyzer; they can
    hold sets, enums and nested rule objects.
    """
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {str(k): _jsonable(v) for k, v in value.items()}
    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
        return [_jsonable(v) for v in value]
    if isinstance(value, set):
        return sorted(_jsonable(v) for v in value)
    if isinstance(value, (str, int, float, bool)) or value is None:
        return value
    if hasattr(value, "value"):        # Enum
        return value.value
    return str(value)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------- runner


def run_analysis(
    source_path: Path,
    *,
    vendor: Optional[str],
    report_path: Path,
    progress: Callable[[str], None] = lambda _step: None,
) -> Tuple[Dict[str, Any], List[Dict[str, Any]], List[Dict[str, Any]]]:
    """Parse, analyze and render one ruleset.

    Returns `(meta, findings, rules)` where meta carries the summary, statistics
    and zone matrix. Raises on any failure; the caller records it on the row.
    """
    progress("Reading input file")
    csv_path = to_csv(source_path)

    manager = ConfigurationManager()
    zone_config = manager.load_zone_config(None)
    analysis_config = manager.load_analysis_config(str(config.ANALYSIS_CONFIG))
    handler = get_appid_handler()

    vendor_type = VendorType(vendor) if vendor else None

    # The analyzers narrate to stdout; keep that out of the server log but hold
    # on to it so a failed run can show what it managed to do.
    captured = io.StringIO()

    progress("Parsing rules")
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(captured):
        parser = MultiVendorCSVParser(
            vendor_type=vendor_type,
            config_manager=manager,
            use_hashed=False,
            debug=False,
            app_id_handler=handler,
        )
        rules = parser.parse_csv(str(csv_path))

    if not rules:
        raise ValueError("No rules were parsed from the file. Check that it is a rule export.")

    progress(f"Analyzing {len(rules)} rules")
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(captured):
        analyzer = EnhancedFirewallRuleAnalyzer(
            zone_config=zone_config,
            config_manager=manager,
            analysis_config=analysis_config,
            app_id_handler=handler,
        )
        results = analyzer.analyze_rules(rules)

    progress("Generating report")
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(captured):
        generator = EnhancedHTMLReportGenerator(detailed_mode=True, group_by_name=False)
        generator.generate_report(results, str(report_path))

    stats = results["statistics"]
    detected_vendor = rules[0].vendor_type.value if rules else "unknown"

    meta = {
        "vendor": detected_vendor,
        "summary": _jsonable(results["summary"]),
        "stats": _jsonable(
            {
                **{k: v for k, v in stats.items() if k != "zone_summary"},
                "findings_by_type": dict(stats.get("findings_by_type", {})),
                "findings_by_risk": dict(stats.get("findings_by_risk", {})),
                "vendor_distribution": dict(stats.get("vendor_distribution", {})),
            }
        ),
        "zone_summary": _jsonable(results.get("zone_summary", {})),
        "log": captured.getvalue()[-8000:],
    }

    findings = [_finding_dict(f) for f in results["findings"]]

    # Every rule in the file, so the Rule Explorer can show disabled and
    # filtered-out rules too - not just the ones that reached the analyzers.
    analyzed = {id(r): r for r in results.get("rules", [])}
    all_rules = results.get("all_rules", rules)
    rule_rows = [_rule_dict(analyzed.get(id(r), r), i + 1) for i, r in enumerate(all_rules)]

    return meta, findings, rule_rows
```

## `src/firewall_analyzer/webui/store.py`

```python
"""SQLite persistence.

Plain `sqlite3` rather than an ORM: the schema is five tables, the analyzer has
no runtime dependencies, and keeping it that way means the API installs with
three packages. Findings and rules land in real tables (not a JSON blob) so the
Findings and Rule Explorer pages can filter, sort and paginate server-side.
"""

import json
import sqlite3
import threading
from contextlib import contextmanager
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Any, Dict, Iterator, List, Optional

from . import config

_local = threading.local()

SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS projects (
    id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    name        TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    created_at  TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS analyses (
    id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    project_id    TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    label         TEXT NOT NULL,
    vendor        TEXT,
    filename      TEXT NOT NULL,
    source_path   TEXT NOT NULL,
    status        TEXT NOT NULL,          -- queued | running | succeeded | failed
    progress      TEXT,                   -- human-readable current step
    error         TEXT,
    created_at    TEXT NOT NULL,
    started_at    TEXT,
    finished_at   TEXT,
    summary       TEXT,                   -- json
    stats         TEXT,                   -- json
    zone_summary  TEXT,                   -- json
    report_path   TEXT
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_analyses_project ON analyses(project_id, created_at DESC);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS findings (
    id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    analysis_id    TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES analyses(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    rule_id        TEXT,
    rule_name      TEXT,
    issue_type     TEXT,
    risk_level     TEXT,
    score          INTEGER,
    description    TEXT,
    recommendation TEXT,
    formula        TEXT,
    details        TEXT                   -- json
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_findings_analysis ON findings(analysis_id, score DESC);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_findings_risk     ON findings(analysis_id, risk_level);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS rules (
    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    analysis_id   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES analyses(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    seq           INTEGER,
    rule_id       TEXT,
    name          TEXT,
    action        TEXT,
    disabled      INTEGER,
    src_zones     TEXT,
    dst_zones     TEXT,
    src_addresses TEXT,
    dst_addresses TEXT,
    services      TEXT,
    applications  TEXT,
    logging       TEXT,
    rule_usage    TEXT,
    risk_score    INTEGER,
    finding_count INTEGER,
    raw           TEXT                    -- json
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_rules_analysis ON rules(analysis_id, risk_score DESC);
"""


def connect() -> sqlite3.Connection:
    """One connection per thread; SQLite objects are not shareable across them."""
    conn = getattr(_local, "conn", None)
    if conn is None:
        config.ensure_dirs()
        conn = sqlite3.connect(config.DB_PATH, timeout=30)
        conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
        conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
        _local.conn = conn
    return conn


@contextmanager
def tx() -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:
    conn = connect()
    try:
        yield conn
        conn.commit()
    except Exception:
        conn.rollback()
        raise


def init_db() -> None:
    with tx() as conn:
        conn.executescript(SCHEMA)


def now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")


def _loads(value: Optional[str]) -> Any:
    return json.loads(value) if value else None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- projects


def upsert_project(project_id: str, name: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    with tx() as conn:
        existing = conn.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM projects WHERE name = ?", (name,)
        ).fetchone()
        if existing:
            return dict(existing)
        conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO projects (id, name, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
            (project_id, name, now()),
        )
    return {"id": project_id, "name": name, "created_at": now()}


def list_projects() -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    rows = connect().execute(
        """
        SELECT p.*,
               (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM analyses a WHERE a.project_id = p.id) AS analysis_count
        FROM projects p ORDER BY p.created_at DESC
        """
    ).fetchall()
    return [dict(r) for r in rows]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- analyses


def create_analysis(record: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    cols = ", ".join(record)
    marks = ", ".join("?" for _ in record)
    with tx() as conn:
        conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO analyses ({cols}) VALUES ({marks})", tuple(record.values()))


def update_analysis(analysis_id: str, **fields: Any) -> None:
    if not fields:
        return
    assignments = ", ".join(f"{k} = ?" for k in fields)
    with tx() as conn:
        conn.execute(
            f"UPDATE analyses SET {assignments} WHERE id = ?",
            (*fields.values(), analysis_id),
        )


def get_analysis(analysis_id: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
    row = connect().execute(
        """
        SELECT a.*, p.name AS project_name
        FROM analyses a JOIN projects p ON p.id = a.project_id
        WHERE a.id = ?
        """,
        (analysis_id,),
    ).fetchone()
    if not row:
        return None
    record = dict(row)
    for key in ("summary", "stats", "zone_summary"):
        record[key] = _loads(record.get(key))
    return record


def list_analyses(limit: int = 50, project_id: Optional[str] = None) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    sql = """
        SELECT a.id, a.label, a.vendor, a.filename, a.status, a.progress, a.error,
               a.created_at, a.finished_at, a.summary, a.stats, p.name AS project_name
        FROM analyses a JOIN projects p ON p.id = a.project_id
    """
    params: List[Any] = []
    if project_id:
        sql += " WHERE a.project_id = ?"
        params.append(project_id)
    sql += " ORDER BY a.created_at DESC LIMIT ?"
    params.append(limit)

    out = []
    for row in connect().execute(sql, params).fetchall():
        record = dict(row)
        record["summary"] = _loads(record.get("summary"))
        record["stats"] = _loads(record.get("stats"))
        out.append(record)
    return out


def delete_analysis(analysis_id: str) -> bool:
    with tx() as conn:
        cur = conn.execute("DELETE FROM analyses WHERE id = ?", (analysis_id,))
    return cur.rowcount > 0


# ------------------------------------------------------- findings and rules


def insert_findings(analysis_id: str, findings: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
    if not findings:
        return
    with tx() as conn:
        conn.executemany(
            """INSERT INTO findings
               (analysis_id, rule_id, rule_name, issue_type, risk_level, score,
                description, recommendation, formula, details)
               VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
            [
                (
                    analysis_id, f["rule_id"], f["rule_name"], f["issue_type"],
                    f["risk_level"], f["score"], f["description"],
                    f["recommendation"], f.get("formula", ""),
                    json.dumps(f.get("details") or {}),
                )
                for f in findings
            ],
        )


def insert_rules(analysis_id: str, rules: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
    if not rules:
        return
    with tx() as conn:
        conn.executemany(
            """INSERT INTO rules
               (analysis_id, seq, rule_id, name, action, disabled, src_zones, dst_zones,
                src_addresses, dst_addresses, services, applications, logging,
                rule_usage, risk_score, finding_count, raw)
               VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
            [
                (
                    analysis_id, r["seq"], r["rule_id"], r["name"], r["action"],
                    int(r["disabled"]), json.dumps(r["src_zones"]), json.dumps(r["dst_zones"]),
                    json.dumps(r["src_addresses"]), json.dumps(r["dst_addresses"]),
                    json.dumps(r["services"]), json.dumps(r["applications"]),
                    r.get("logging", ""), r.get("rule_usage", ""),
                    r["risk_score"], r["finding_count"], json.dumps(r.get("raw") or {}),
                )
                for r in rules
            ],
        )


#: Sort keys the API will accept, mapped to real columns. Anything not in this
#: map is rejected, so the value never reaches the SQL string.
FINDING_SORTS = {
    "score": "score", "risk": "risk_level", "rule": "rule_name", "type": "issue_type",
}
RULE_SORTS = {
    "risk": "risk_score", "name": "name", "findings": "finding_count",
    "action": "action", "seq": "seq",
}


def query_findings(
    analysis_id: str,
    *,
    risk: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    issue_type: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    search: Optional[str] = None,
    sort: str = "score",
    direction: str = "desc",
    limit: int = 50,
    offset: int = 0,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    where = ["analysis_id = ?"]
    params: List[Any] = [analysis_id]

    if risk:
        where.append(f"risk_level IN ({','.join('?' * len(risk))})")
        params.extend(risk)
    if issue_type:
        where.append(f"issue_type IN ({','.join('?' * len(issue_type))})")
        params.extend(issue_type)
    if search:
        where.append("(rule_name LIKE ? OR description LIKE ?)")
        params.extend([f"%{search}%"] * 2)

    clause = " AND ".join(where)
    total = connect().execute(
        f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM findings WHERE {clause}", params
    ).fetchone()[0]

    column = FINDING_SORTS.get(sort, "score")
    order = "ASC" if direction == "asc" else "DESC"
    rows = connect().execute(
        f"""SELECT rule_id, rule_name, issue_type, risk_level, score, description,
                   recommendation, formula, details
            FROM findings WHERE {clause}
            ORDER BY {column} {order}, id ASC LIMIT ? OFFSET ?""",
        (*params, limit, offset),
    ).fetchall()

    items = []
    for row in rows:
        item = dict(row)
        item["details"] = _loads(item["details"]) or {}
        items.append(item)
    return {"total": total, "items": items, "limit": limit, "offset": offset}


def query_rules(
    analysis_id: str,
    *,
    action: Optional[str] = None,
    search: Optional[str] = None,
    with_findings_only: bool = False,
    sort: str = "risk",
    direction: str = "desc",
    limit: int = 50,
    offset: int = 0,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    where = ["analysis_id = ?"]
    params: List[Any] = [analysis_id]

    if action:
        where.append("action = ?")
        params.append(action)
    if with_findings_only:
        where.append("finding_count > 0")
    if search:
        where.append("(name LIKE ? OR rule_id LIKE ? OR src_addresses LIKE ? OR dst_addresses LIKE ?)")
        params.extend([f"%{search}%"] * 4)

    clause = " AND ".join(where)
    total = connect().execute(
        f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM rules WHERE {clause}", params
    ).fetchone()[0]

    column = RULE_SORTS.get(sort, "risk_score")
    order = "ASC" if direction == "asc" else "DESC"
    rows = connect().execute(
        f"""SELECT seq, rule_id, name, action, disabled, src_zones, dst_zones,
                   src_addresses, dst_addresses, services, applications, logging,
                   rule_usage, risk_score, finding_count
            FROM rules WHERE {clause}
            ORDER BY {column} {order}, seq ASC LIMIT ? OFFSET ?""",
        (*params, limit, offset),
    ).fetchall()

    items = []
    for row in rows:
        item = dict(row)
        for key in ("src_zones", "dst_zones", "src_addresses", "dst_addresses",
                    "services", "applications"):
            item[key] = _loads(item[key]) or []
        item["disabled"] = bool(item["disabled"])
        items.append(item)
    return {"total": total, "items": items, "limit": limit, "offset": offset}


def rule_detail(analysis_id: str, rule_id: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
    row = connect().execute(
        "SELECT * FROM rules WHERE analysis_id = ? AND rule_id = ? LIMIT 1",
        (analysis_id, rule_id),
    ).fetchone()
    if not row:
        return None
    rule = dict(row)
    for key in ("src_zones", "dst_zones", "src_addresses", "dst_addresses",
                "services", "applications", "raw"):
        rule[key] = _loads(rule[key]) or ([] if key != "raw" else {})
    rule["disabled"] = bool(rule["disabled"])
    rule["findings"] = query_findings(analysis_id, limit=200)["items"]
    rule["findings"] = [f for f in rule["findings"] if f["rule_id"] == rule_id]
    return rule


def finding_facets(analysis_id: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Counts per risk level and issue type, for the filter chips."""
    conn = connect()
    by_risk = {
        r["risk_level"]: r["n"]
        for r in conn.execute(
            "SELECT risk_level, COUNT(*) AS n FROM findings WHERE analysis_id = ? GROUP BY risk_level",
            (analysis_id,),
        )
    }
    by_type = {
        r["issue_type"]: r["n"]
        for r in conn.execute(
            "SELECT issue_type, COUNT(*) AS n FROM findings WHERE analysis_id = ?"
            " GROUP BY issue_type ORDER BY n DESC",
            (analysis_id,),
        )
    }

    # Rules bucketed by the analyzer's own risk thresholds. Counting "rules with
    # any finding" is close to useless here: several analyzers emit a score-1
    # finding to record that a rule is compliant, so nearly every rule has one.
    bands = conn.execute(
        """
        SELECT
          SUM(CASE WHEN risk_score >= 70 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)                    AS high,
          SUM(CASE WHEN risk_score >= 40 AND risk_score < 70 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS medium,
          SUM(CASE WHEN risk_score >  0  AND risk_score < 40 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS low,
          SUM(CASE WHEN risk_score = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)                       AS clean,
          COUNT(*)                                                              AS total
        FROM rules WHERE analysis_id = ? AND disabled = 0
        """,
        (analysis_id,),
    ).fetchone()

    return {
        "by_risk": by_risk,
        "by_type": by_type,
        "rule_bands": {k: (bands[k] or 0) for k in ("high", "medium", "low", "clean", "total")},
    }
```
